API reference#

Sphinx builds this page from the docstrings of the installed package, so it cannot drift from the code. Everything below is public; anything not listed here is internal and may change without notice. The documentation build fails when a public module exports a name that this page does not show.

Package settings#

configure

Set the process-wide numeric settings scatterem is tuned for.
scatterem.configure(*, matmul_precision: str | None = 'medium') → dict[str, str | None]#

Set the process-wide numeric settings scatterem is tuned for.

Nothing is set at import scatterem. Direct reconstructions, simulations and I/O run at whatever the process has – torch’s default "highest" unless the caller changes it. Call this to run them at TF32 speed.

Parameters:

matmul_precision ({"highest", "high", "medium"} or None, default "medium") – Passed to torch.set_float32_matmul_precision(). "medium" and "high" let float32 matmuls and convolutions run in TF32 on Ampere and later GPUs (and, for "medium", in bfloat16 through oneDNN on CPUs that support it): faster, with about three significant digits instead of seven. "highest" is true float32. None leaves the setting untouched.

Returns:

The value every setting had before this call, keyed by parameter name, so configure(**previous) restores them. A value is None when torch could not report it (see Notes); passing that back sets nothing.

Return type:

dict of str to str or None

Raises:

ValueError – If matmul_precision is not one of the three torch knows (torch itself only warns, and sets nothing).

Notes

Change the precision with this function or torch.set_float32_matmul_precision(), never with the legacy flag torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32: torch (2.11) keeps three records of the precision, the flag rewrites two of them, and next to "medium" the third then makes torch.get_float32_matmul_precision() raise for the rest of the process – which some training frameworks call on every CUDA fit. A call here with a precision rewrites all three and repairs that state.

Examples

>>> import torch
>>> import scatterem
>>> previous = scatterem.configure(matmul_precision="high")
>>> torch.get_float32_matmul_precision()
'high'
>>> _ = scatterem.configure(**previous)

class scatterem.data.datasets.Dataset(array: Any, name: str, origin: NDArray | tuple | list | float | int, sampling: NDArray | tuple | list | float | int, units: list[str] | tuple | list, signal_units: str = 'arb. units', _token: object | None = None, device: device | str | None = None)#

An array plus the calibration needed to interpret its axes.

Each axis carries an origin, a pitch and a unit, so a position in the array can be turned into a physical coordinate without the caller tracking the conversion. Values have their own unit, separate from the axes’.

Parameters:

  • array (array-like) – The data itself.

  • name (str) – Label used in reprs and figure titles.

  • origin (numpy.ndarray, tuple, list, float, or int) – Coordinate of index zero on each axis.

  • sampling (numpy.ndarray, tuple, list, float, or int) – Pitch per axis, in units.

  • units (list of str, or tuple) – One unit string per axis.

  • signal_units (str, optional) – Unit of the stored values. Default is “arb. units”.

  • _token (object, optional) – Internal sentinel guarding direct construction; use Dataset.from_array() instead of calling this constructor.

  • device (torch.device or str or None, optional) – None keeps a torch tensor’s device; other inputs become CPU tensors.

Variables:

  • array (torch.Tensor) – The values, as a tensor of any rank.

  • name (str) – Label used in reprs and figure titles.

  • origin (numpy.ndarray) – Coordinate of index zero on each axis.

  • sampling (numpy.ndarray) – Pitch per axis, in units.

  • units (list of str) – One unit string per axis.

  • signal_units (str) – Unit of the stored values.

class scatterem.data.datasets.Dataset4DStem(array: Tensor | ndarray, name: str, origin: NDArray | tuple | list | float | int, sampling: NDArray | tuple | list | float | int, units: list[str] | tuple | list, signal_units: str = 'arb. units', meta: AcquisitionMetadata | None = None, transform_to_amplitudes: bool = False, astype_float32: bool = True, fourier_shift_dim: tuple | None = None, probe_index: int = 0, device: device | str | None = None, normalize: bool = True, clip_neg_values: bool = True, copy: bool = True, _token: object | None = None)#

A 4D STEM dataset with metadata for electron diffraction patterns.

Parameters:

  • array (Tensor) – The 4D diffraction data, shaped (scan_y, scan_x, det_y, det_x).

  • name (str) – The name of the dataset.

  • origin (NDArray or tuple or list or float or int) – The per-axis origin, i.e. the pixel offset of the array’s zero index.

  • sampling (NDArray or tuple or list or float or int) – The per-axis physical sampling (scan step and detector pixel size).

  • units (list of str or tuple or list) – The per-axis physical units.

  • signal_units (str) – The units of the recorded signal.

  • meta (AcquisitionMetadata, optional) – Acquisition metadata (energy, semiconvergence angle, aberrations, and related quantities).

  • transform_to_amplitudes (bool) – Whether to take the square root of the array in place, converting recorded intensities to amplitudes.

  • astype_float32 (bool) – Whether to cast the array to float32.

  • fourier_shift_dim (tuple, optional) – Detector dims to fftshift on construction: only to centre corner data.

  • probe_index (int) – Index of the probe this dataset is associated with.

  • device (torch.device or str or None, optional) – None keeps a torch tensor’s device; other inputs become CPU.

  • normalize (bool) – Whether to divide the array in place by the maximum mean diffraction pattern. Default is True. This rescales the stored data: pass normalize=False (and clip_neg_values=False) whenever raw counts must survive byte-exact, e.g. for dose accounting or comparisons against another reader.

  • clip_neg_values (bool) – Whether to clamp negative values to zero in place. Default is True; see the note on normalize.

  • copy (bool) – Whether to clone the array before the in-place operations above run, so that the caller’s array is never mutated.

  • _token (object, optional) – Sentinel guarding direct construction; use from_array() instead.

Variables:

bright_field_mask_threshold (float) – Default bright-field mask level, 0.3. FusedFullFieldConfig reads it when the caller omits the threshold; the other configs have their own default. The examples pass it to every config; set it per dataset.

bright_field_radius_and_center(estimator: Literal['integral', 'rayfit'] = 'integral', *, edge_reach: float | None = None, arc_floor: float | None = None) → PupilEstimate#

Return the radius and centre (y, x) of the bright-field disk [pixel].

Calls scatterem.data.pupil_gauge.measure_pupil() on the mean diffraction pattern. The largest plausible radius is the default of that function (0.45 of the shorter detector side), or 1.0 for a dataset that is cropped to the bright field (is_bright_field).

Parameters:

  • estimator ({"integral", "rayfit"}) – "integral" (default) for a complete disk. "rayfit" for a disk with a missing sector or with a part outside the detector.

  • edge_reach (float, optional) – Half-width of the edge band [pixel]; None: 2 (integral) or 10 (rayfit). A wide band reads a sloped disk top 4 % small (Gd2O3). Raise for soft edges.

  • arc_floor (float, optional) – Only for "rayfit": the smallest fraction of the full circle that the accepted edge points must cover.

Returns:

(rim_radius, rim_center): the radius [pixel] and the centre (y, x) [pixel] as a NumPy array of shape (2,).

Return type:

PupilEstimate

Raises:

ValueError – If the mean pattern has no clear disk; see measure_pupil().

calibrate_reciprocal_from_bright_field(semiconvergence_angle: float | None = None, estimator: Literal['integral', 'rayfit'] = 'integral', *, edge_reach: float | None = None) → float#

Calibrate the reciprocal-space pixel size dk from the bright field.

Sets dk = alpha / rBF / wavelength and self.sampling = (dr, dr, dk, dk) in place (the setter updates self.meta.sampling). rBF comes from the mean pattern of the whole detector (bright_field_radius_and_center()). A scratch crop (as crop_brightfield_, same edge_reach, no normalisation, so the array does not change) recentres the detector entries of self.origin, sets self._radius_bright_field and refuses a disk near the detector edge.

Parameters:

  • semiconvergence_angle (float, optional) – Beam convergence semi-angle in radians. Defaults to self.meta.semiconvergence_angle.

  • estimator ({"integral", "rayfit"}) – The disk estimator; see bright_field_radius_and_center().

  • edge_reach (float, optional) – See bright_field_radius_and_center().

Returns:

The calibrated reciprocal-space sampling dk.

Return type:

float

classmethod from_array(array: Any, name: str | None = None, origin: NDArray | tuple | list | float | int | None = None, sampling: NDArray | tuple | list | float | int | None = None, units: list[str] | tuple | list | None = None, signal_units: str = 'arb. units', meta: AcquisitionMetadata | None = None, transform_to_amplitudes: bool = False, fourier_shift_dim: tuple | None = None, normalize: bool = True, clip_neg_values: bool = True, copy: bool = True, *, device: device | str | None = None, is_cropped: bool = False, out_of_core: bool = False, ooc_row_block: int = 8, g_residency: str = 'auto', energy: float | None = None, semiconvergence_angle: float | None = None, scan_step: float | tuple | list | NDArray | None = None, reciprocal_step: float | tuple | list | NDArray | None = None, rotation: float = 0.0, aberrations: Aberrations | None = None) → Dataset4DStem#

Build a 4D-STEM dataset (scan y, scan x, detector y, detector x).

Parameters:

  • array (Any) – The 4D cube: numpy array, tensor, h5py dataset or memory map.

  • name (str, optional) – Label. Default: "4d dataset".

  • origin (NDArray or tuple or list or float or int, optional) – Coordinate of index zero per axis. Default: 0, or the array centre on the physics path (see energy).

  • sampling (NDArray or tuple or list or float or int, optional) – Pitch per axis. Defaults to what meta describes (meta.sampling), else 1.0 per axis.

  • units (list of str or tuple or list, optional) – Unit per axis. Default: the units of meta, else "pixels".

  • signal_units (str) – Unit of the values.

  • meta (AcquisitionMetadata, optional) – Acquisition metadata. Built internally from the physics-path parameters below when None and energy is given.

  • transform_to_amplitudes (bool) – Whether to take the square root of the array in place, converting recorded intensities to amplitudes.

  • fourier_shift_dim (tuple, optional) – Detector dimensions to fftshift in place on construction.

  • normalize (bool) – Whether to divide the array in place by the maximum mean diffraction pattern. Default is True. This rescales the stored data: pass normalize=False (and clip_neg_values=False) whenever raw counts must survive byte-exact, e.g. for dose accounting or comparisons against another reader.

  • clip_neg_values (bool) – Whether to clamp negative values to zero in place. Default is True; see the note on normalize.

  • copy (bool) – Whether to clone the array before any in-place operations run, so that the caller’s array is never mutated.

  • device (torch.device or str or None, optional) – None keeps a torch tensor’s device; other inputs become CPU. Out-of-core: compute device for streamed slabs (None → CPU).

  • is_cropped (bool) – Whether the array is the result of a crop.

  • out_of_core (bool) – Keep the cube where it is and read it in pieces (a MemmapSource); every read converts like the eager path. uint8, uint16 and float16 cubes stream in a fit.

  • ooc_row_block (int) – Scan rows per read of pass 0 and iter_scan_blocks (out-of-core only).

  • g_residency (str) – "gpu" | "vbf_gpu" | "cpu_pinned" | "auto" – where the streaming vBF provider keeps G (out-of-core only).

  • energy (float, optional) – Beam energy in eV. Triggers the physics convenience path: when meta is None and energy is given, an AcquisitionMetadata is built internally (shape derived from array, sampling = (dr, dr, dk, dk) with dr from scan_step and dk from reciprocal_step – both scalar or a length-2 pair, dk defaulting to a (1.0, 1.0) placeholder to be calibrated later, e.g. via calibrate_reciprocal_from_bright_field). origin defaults to the array center in this path when not given explicitly.

  • semiconvergence_angle (float, optional) – Beam convergence semi-angle in radians, used by the physics path.

  • scan_step (float or tuple or list or NDArray, optional) – Real-space scan step, used by the physics path.

  • reciprocal_step (float or tuple or list or NDArray, optional) – Reciprocal-space pixel size, used by the physics path.

  • rotation (float) – Scan rotation in degrees, used by the physics path.

  • aberrations (Aberrations, optional) – Aberration coefficients, used by the physics path.

Returns:

The container, with any unset axis metadata filled in from the array’s rank.

Return type:

Dataset4DStem

classmethod load(path: str | Path, *, device: str | device = 'cpu')#

Read an instance of cls (or of a subclass) from path.

Parameters:

  • path (str or pathlib.Path) – A file written by save().

  • device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device every tensor field is placed on. Default "cpu".

Returns:

The object. When the file holds a subclass of cls that declares its own schema, an instance of that subclass.

Return type:

Serializable

Raises:

SerializationError – The file holds an unrelated class, a schema version this code cannot read, or a field list that does not match the class’s.

save(path: str | Path, *, overwrite: bool = False) → Path#

Write every declared field to one HDF5 file.

Parameters:

  • path (str or pathlib.Path) – File to write. Missing parent directories are created.

  • overwrite (bool, optional) – Replace an existing file. Default False, which refuses.

Returns:

The path written.

Return type:

pathlib.Path

Raises:

SerializationError – If the file exists and overwrite is false, or if a declared field cannot be written.

class scatterem.data.datasets.DatasetVirtualBrightField4DStem(array: Tensor, name: str, origin: NDArray | tuple | list | float | int, sampling: NDArray | tuple | list | float | int, units: list[str] | tuple | list, parent_dataset: Dataset4DStem | None = None, diffraction_pattern_mean_normalized: torch.Tensor = tensor([]), bright_field_mask: torch.Tensor = tensor([]), bright_field_inds: torch.Tensor = tensor([]), bright_field_inds_centered: torch.Tensor = tensor([]), bright_field_inds_radial_order: torch.Tensor = tensor([]), bright_field_inds_ordered_by_radius: torch.Tensor = tensor([]), bright_field_inds_centered_ordered_by_radius: torch.Tensor = tensor([]), k: torch.Tensor = tensor([]), qx_1d: torch.Tensor = tensor([]), qy_1d: torch.Tensor = tensor([]), signal_units: str = 'arb. units', meta: AcquisitionMetadata | None = None, astype_float32: bool = True, fourier_shift_dim: tuple | None = None, probe_index: int = 0, device: torch.device | str | None = None, clip_neg_values: bool = True, _token: object | None = None)#

A virtual bright field 4D STEM dataset with metadata for electron diffraction patterns.

Parameters:

  • array (torch.Tensor) – Gathered bright-field diffraction data, shape (Ry, Rx, N_bf).

  • name (str) – Dataset name.

  • origin (numpy.typing.NDArray or tuple or list or float or int) – Real-space origin.

  • sampling (numpy.typing.NDArray or tuple or list or float or int) – Real-space sampling (pixel size) per axis.

  • units (list of str or tuple or list) – Units of each axis.

  • parent_dataset (Dataset4DStem or None, optional) – 4D-STEM dataset this virtual bright field was derived from.

  • diffraction_pattern_mean_normalized (torch.Tensor, optional) – Max-normalized mean CBED used to build the bright-field mask.

  • bright_field_mask (torch.Tensor, optional) – Boolean bright-field detector mask.

  • bright_field_inds (torch.Tensor, optional) – Detector pixel indices inside the bright-field mask.

  • bright_field_inds_centered (torch.Tensor, optional) – bright_field_inds centered on their mean.

  • bright_field_inds_radial_order (torch.Tensor, optional) – Permutation sorting bright_field_inds by radius.

  • bright_field_inds_ordered_by_radius (torch.Tensor, optional) – bright_field_inds sorted by radius.

  • bright_field_inds_centered_ordered_by_radius (torch.Tensor, optional) – bright_field_inds_centered sorted by radius.

  • k (torch.Tensor, optional) – Physical detector k-vectors of the bright-field pixels.

  • qx_1d (torch.Tensor, optional) – 1D Fourier frequencies along the scan x-axis.

  • qy_1d (torch.Tensor, optional) – 1D Fourier frequencies along the scan y-axis.

  • signal_units (str, optional) – Units of the signal values.

  • meta (AcquisitionMetadata or None, optional) – Acquisition metadata.

  • astype_float32 (bool, optional) – If True (default), cast the array to float32.

  • fourier_shift_dim (tuple, optional) – Dimensions to ifftshift; unused here (always None from from_4dstem_dataset()).

  • probe_index (int, optional) – Probe index for multi-probe datasets.

  • device (torch.device or str or None, optional) – None keeps a torch tensor’s device; other inputs become CPU.

  • clip_neg_values (bool, optional) – If True (default), clip negative array values to zero.

  • _token (object or None, optional) – Internal construction guard.

scatterem.data.datasets.with_meta(dataset: D, meta: Any) → D#

A cheap view of dataset that reads meta instead of its own.

The view is a shallow copy: it shares the measurement array and every other attribute with dataset, so it costs one attribute dictionary. Only meta differs, and the view starts with an empty virtual-bright- field cache, so a get_vbf on it builds a provider under meta. dataset itself is not changed.

Use it to reconstruct the same data with other metadata, for example two aberration fits:

view = with_meta(dataset, fit.applied_to(dataset.meta))
vbf = view.get_vbf(0.5)

scatterem.reconstruction.run() takes meta= and does this for you.

Parameters:

  • dataset (object) – A dataset with a settable meta (a Dataset4DStem, …).

  • meta (object) – The metadata the view reads. It is bound by reference, not copied, as an assignment dataset.meta = meta would bind it.

Returns:

The view, of the same type as dataset.

Return type:

object

Raises:

TypeError – If dataset has no meta attribute or it cannot be set.

Running a reconstruction#

run

Run the reconstruction config selects on data.

Result

Base of every reconstruction result.

ReconstructionConfig

Base of every reconstruction config.

Provenance

Where a Result came from.

register_runner

Register the function run() calls for config_type.
scatterem.reconstruction.run(data: Any, config: ReconstructionConfig[R], *, reuse: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, meta: Any = None) → R#

Run the reconstruction config selects on data.

The family is chosen by type(config) (the nearest registered class in its MRO). data and data.meta are never written to; outputs are placed on data.device or, for a runner that departs from that rule (see the module docstring), where provenance.device says.

To compare two aberration fits on one dataset, pass each fit’s metadata:

a = run(ds, config, meta=fit_a.applied_to(ds.meta))
b = run(ds, config, meta=fit_b.applied_to(ds.meta))
Parameters:

  • data (object) – The input the family expects (a dataset, a series, …).

  • config (ReconstructionConfig) – The family’s frozen config.

  • reuse (Mapping, optional) – Intermediate products from earlier runs, by the key the family documents (for example a virtual bright field). Nothing is reused unless it is passed here.

  • meta (object, optional) – Metadata to use instead of data.meta. The runner gets a with_meta() view of data: it shares the array, starts with an empty vBF cache and leaves data unchanged. The result’s provenance.meta_override is True. A reused vBF ("vbf" / "vbf_cache") must have been built under this meta, for example with_meta(data, meta).get_vbf(t).

Returns:

The family’s result type, as config’s type parameter declares.

Return type:

Result

Raises:

  • TypeError – If config is not a ReconstructionConfig, if no runner is registered for its type, or if the runner does not return a Result.

  • ValueError – If reuse holds a key the family does not accept, or, with meta, a vBF provider built under other metadata.

Warns:

UserWarning – If data is 4D-STEM data whose reciprocal sampling dk is still the (1.0, 1.0) placeholder of Dataset4DStem.from_array.

class scatterem.reconstruction.Result(*, provenance: Provenance, diagnostics: Mapping[str, ~typing.Any]=<factory>)#

Base of every reconstruction result.

A family’s result adds its named outputs as fields and implements as_tuple(), which returns exactly what the family’s older function returned, so a caller can switch entry point without changing a number. Results compare by identity: their fields are tensors.

Parameters:

  • provenance (Provenance) – Where the result came from.

  • diagnostics (Mapping, optional) – Secondary outputs a family reports beside its named ones (read-only; empty by default).

class scatterem.reconstruction.ReconstructionConfig#

Base of every reconstruction config.

A family subclasses it as a frozen dataclass whose fields and defaults are exactly the keyword arguments of the function it wraps, parameterised by its result type (ReconstructionConfig[DirectPtychographyResult]) so run() is typed per family, and sets the class attribute method.

class scatterem.reconstruction.Provenance(method: str, config: Mapping[str, Any], scatterem_version: str, input_name: str | None, meta: Any | None, device: device, meta_override: bool = False)#

Where a Result came from.

Deliberately free of a timestamp or git SHA: either would make two identical runs differ, and golden tests compare results field by field.

Parameters:

  • method (str) – The reconstruction family, the config type’s method.

  • config (Mapping) – The fully resolved config, one entry per config field (read-only).

  • scatterem_version (str) – scatterem.__version__ at the time of the run.

  • input_name (str or None) – The input’s name, when it has a string one.

  • meta (object or None) – A detached snapshot copy of the input’s meta: later changes to the input’s metadata do not reach it, and it holds no autograd graph.

  • device (torch.device) – The device the input lived on, where the outputs are placed.

  • meta_override (bool, optional) – True when the run read metadata other than the dataset’s own (run(..., meta=...) or a with_meta() view); meta is then that metadata. Default False.

Register the function run() calls for config_type.

Used as a decorator in the module that implements the family. The runner is called as runner(data, config, reuse), with reuse a read-only mapping holding only keys from reuse_keys.

Parameters:

  • config_type (type) – A ReconstructionConfig subclass that sets method.

  • reuse_keys (sequence of str, optional) – The reuse= keys this family accepts; run() rejects others.

Returns:

A decorator that registers its argument and returns it unchanged.

callable

Raises:

  • TypeError – If config_type is not a ReconstructionConfig subclass with a string method.

  • ValueError – If config_type already has a runner.

class scatterem.reconstruction.ptychography.direct.AberrationFitConfig(correction_method: str = 'combined', fit_rotation: bool = False, target_percentage_nonzero_pixels: float = 0.75, n_batches: int = 25, registration_upsample_factor: int = 10, lowpass_fwhm_bright_field: float | None = None, bin_factors: tuple[int, ...] = (2, 1, 1), verbosity: int = 0, correct_order: int = 1, gradient_mask: tuple[bool, ...] | None = None, num_iterations: int = 10, lr: float = 20, bright_field_mask_threshold: float = 0.5, roi_shape: tuple[int, int] = (128, 128), roi_center: str | tuple[int, int] = 'center', upsample: int | str = 'nyquist', update_dataset: bool = True, n_center_indices: int = 25, phase_sign: Literal['preserve', 'positive', 'negative'] = 'preserve', sharpness_metric: str = 'sparsity', reg_weight: float = 0.05, alignment_method: str = 'reference', peak_selection: Literal['argmax', 'guided'] = 'argmax', init_method: Literal['closed_form', 'zeros'] = 'closed_form', use_com_rotation_prior: Literal['auto', 'off'] = 'auto', check_defocus_sign: bool = False)#

The aberration fit on a 4D-STEM dataset, run through run().

Fields are the keyword arguments of scatterem.reconstruction.ptychography.direct.determine_aberrations(); see it for their meaning. update_dataset keeps its old effect on the fit itself (whether it records the rotation, the defocus guess and the coefficients on the metadata, here reported in AberrationFitResult.meta_updates); run() writes nothing.

data is a Dataset4DStem or a DatasetVirtualBrightField4DStem.

Parameters:

  • correction_method (str) – "combined", "bright-field-shifts" or "autofocus".

  • fit_rotation (bool) – Whether to fit the scan rotation.

  • target_percentage_nonzero_pixels (float) – Target percentage of nonzero pixels for the bright field.

  • n_batches (int) – Number of bright-field batches of the SSB images of the defocus sign check and the autofocus (TV) step; not used by the bright-field shift fit.

  • registration_upsample_factor (int) – Upsampling factor for the shift registration.

  • lowpass_fwhm_bright_field (float or None) – FWHM of the lowpass filter applied to the bright field.

  • bin_factors (tuple of int) – Bin factors for the bright field.

  • verbosity (int) – Verbosity level.

  • correct_order (int) – Order of the aberrations the autofocus stage corrects.

  • gradient_mask (tuple of bool or None) – Which of the 12 coefficients the autofocus may adjust; None means all of them.

  • num_iterations (int) – Number of autofocus iterations.

  • lr (float) – Learning rate of the autofocus optimizer.

  • bright_field_mask_threshold (float) – Bright-field mask threshold.

  • roi_shape (tuple of int) – Shape of the region of interest.

  • roi_center (str or tuple of int) – Center of the region of interest.

  • upsample (int or str) – Upsampling factor, or "nyquist".

  • update_dataset (bool) – Whether the fit records its results on the (copied) metadata.

  • n_center_indices (int) – Number of center indices for the bright-field shift fit.

  • phase_sign ({"preserve", "positive", "negative"}) – Sign convention for the fitted phase.

  • sharpness_metric (str) – Autofocus objective, "sparsity" or "tv".

  • reg_weight (float) – L2 regularization weight toward the seed in the autofocus.

  • alignment_method (str) – Alignment method of the bright-field shift fit.

  • peak_selection ({"argmax", "guided"}) – Which cross-correlation peak is each bright-field shift. Use "guided" on crystals: their correlation is multi-peaked, and the global maximum ("argmax") can pick a lattice copy and flip the sign of C10.

  • init_method ({"closed_form", "zeros"}) – Seed of the bright-field-shift fit.

  • use_com_rotation_prior ({"auto", "off"}) – Whether an unset meta.rotation is seeded from the diffraction centre of mass.

  • check_defocus_sign (bool) – Whether the fit compares the corrected image at the fitted coefficients and at their negative, and keeps the more coherent one. The result then carries the decision in diagnostics["defocus_sign_check"]. Off by default: it costs two passes over the bright-field stack and can change the fit.

class scatterem.reconstruction.ptychography.direct.AberrationFitResult(*, provenance: ~scatterem.reconstruction._runner.Provenance, diagnostics: ~collections.abc.Mapping[str, ~typing.Any] = <factory>, aberrations: ~torch.Tensor, meta_updates: ~collections.abc.Mapping[str, ~typing.Any], rotation: float | None = None)#

Result of AberrationFitConfig.

Parameters:

  • provenance (Provenance) – Where the result came from.

  • diagnostics (Mapping, optional) – {"vbf_cache": ...} when the run was given one to carry through, and {"defocus_sign_check": {...}} when check_defocus_sign was set: c10_fitted, c10_kept, energy_fitted, energy_flipped and flipped. Empty otherwise.

  • aberrations (torch.Tensor) – The 12 fitted aberration coefficients.

  • meta_updates (Mapping) – The metadata attributes the fit changed, by name, with their new values (read-only): what the older entry point wrote onto dataset.meta through the shared vBF.meta. With update_dataset=True these are aberrations, rotation and defocus_guess (reset to 0.0: the fitted defocus is in aberrations[0]).

  • rotation (float or None, optional) – The scan rotation (deg) the aberrations hold at: the fitted one with fit_rotation, else the rotation the fit held. It is set also with update_dataset=False, which writes no meta. None when the fit did not report one.

as_tuple() → tuple[Tensor]#

Return (aberrations,): the fitted tensor wrapped in a 1-tuple.

Returns:

The fitted coefficients, wrapped in a 1-tuple.

Return type:

tuple of torch.Tensor

applied_to(meta: Any) → Any#

Return a new copy of meta with this fit applied.

The copy gets every entry of meta_updates and a new Aberrations holding aberrations, with defocus_guess set to 0.0: the fitted C10 is in aberrations[0] alone, also when the fit ran with update_dataset=False. When meta_updates has no rotation (update_dataset=False, or a held rotation), the copy gets rotation, so the aberrations keep the rotation they hold at. meta itself is not modified, and the copy shares no tensor with this result.

Parameters:

meta (object) – The metadata to start from, typically the fitted data’s own.

Returns:

The updated copy.

Return type:

object

class scatterem.reconstruction.ptychography.direct.DirectPtychographyConfig(upsample: float | str = 'nyquist', bright_field_mask_threshold: float = 0.5, verbosity: int = 0, n_batches: int = 25, return_snr: bool = False, phase_sign: Literal['preserve', 'positive', 'negative'] = 'preserve', ssnr_method: str = 'analytical', gamma_weighting: Literal['phase', 'wiener'] = 'phase', wiener_alpha: float = 0.001, snr_blur_sigma: float = 0.0, rolloff_start: float | None = None)#

Single-side-band direct ptychography, run through run().

Fields and defaults are those of scatterem.reconstruction.ptychography.direct.direct_ptychography(); see it for their meaning. snr_blur_sigma is the one keyword that function takes through **kwargs (used by the empirical SSNR).

data is a Dataset4DStem or an already-built DatasetVirtualBrightField4DStem. reuse={"vbf": provider} supplies a vBF built at this config’s bright_field_mask_threshold from the same dataset, instead of building one; it is not checked against the threshold.

Parameters:

  • upsample (float or str) – Upsampling factor, or "nyquist".

  • bright_field_mask_threshold (float) – Bright-field mask threshold.

  • verbosity (int) – Verbosity level.

  • n_batches (int) – Number of bright-field chunks.

  • return_snr (bool) – Whether to compute the SSNR.

  • phase_sign ({"preserve", "positive", "negative"}) – Global phase-sign convention.

  • ssnr_method (str) – "analytical" or "empirical".

  • gamma_weighting ({"phase", "wiener"}) – How Gamma(Q, K) weights each bright-field pixel.

  • wiener_alpha (float) – Tikhonov floor for gamma_weighting="wiener".

  • snr_blur_sigma (float) – Blur sigma of the empirical SSNR.

  • rolloff_start (float or None) – When set, the phase spectrum is rolled off with a raised cosine from rolloff_start * 2 alpha / lambda to zero at 2 alpha / lambda, the transfer limit of direct ptychography, where the noise makes a bright rim in the spectrum (see rolloff_2alpha()). Typical value 0.9. The SSNR map is not changed. Default is None, no roll-off.

class scatterem.reconstruction.ptychography.direct.DirectPtychographyResult(*, provenance: Provenance, diagnostics: Mapping[str, ~typing.Any]=<factory>, phase: Tensor, ssnr: Tensor | None, sampling: Sampling)#

Bright-field parallax#

measure_bf_parallax

Measure the translation of every BF image.

fit_aberrations_and_rotation_to_bright_field_shifts

Fit the aberrations and rotation to the bright field shifts.

aberrations_and_rotation_from_bright_field_shifts

First determine the bright field shifts, then fit aberrations and rotation.
scatterem.reconstruction.ptychography.direct.measure_bf_parallax(image_spectra, detector_coords_px, *, shift_estimator: str = 'mean_template', binning: int = 1, peak_grid_divisor: int = 20, lowpass_sigma_px: float | None = None, start_template=None, n_refinements: int = 2, peak_tolerance: float = 0.02, remove_image_mean: bool = True, status_line: bool = False, quiet: bool = False) → Tensor#

Measure the translation of every BF image.

Parameters:

  • image_spectra (Tensor, numpy.ndarray or SpectrumSource) – The 2-D Fourier transforms of the N BF images (convention of the module docstring): a complex stack (N, n0, n1), or a source that delivers them in parts (SpectrumSource, ChunkedSpectrumSource).

  • detector_coords_px (array_like) – Real (N, 2) detector coordinates in pixels, relative to the BF disc centre, in the order of the images. Finite, no duplicate rows.

  • shift_estimator ({"mean_template", "neighbour_mesh"}, optional) – "mean_template": common reference; starting reference = the mean of all (binned) spectra, which is the incoherent BF image with the best signal-to-noise ratio; then n_refinements rebuilds as the aligned average. "neighbour_mesh": register detector neighbours (|Δq| <= 1.5 p, p the detector pitch; bins: indices within one) onto each other and solve the least-squares fit of s_j − s_i = d_ij. Use it when a large aberration blurs the mean. It also recovers shifts larger than half the lattice repeat on a periodic specimen, with binning=1, provided the shift difference between detector neighbours stays below half the lattice repeat and the neighbour graph is connected.

  • binning (int, optional) – Detector binning factor (>= 1). Bins are centred on multiples of binning · p; a bin spectrum is the mean of its members. Each BF pixel then gets a shift by a quadratic moving least-squares fit over the bins (Gaussian weights of width binning · p), so every pixel gets a finite shift. 1 means no binning.

  • peak_grid_divisor (int, optional) – The final peak grid is 1/peak_grid_divisor scan pixel. Default 20: a grid error of at most 0.025 px before the parabolic step.

  • lowpass_sigma_px (float, optional) – Gaussian low-pass exp(−2π² σ² |k|²) on every image; σ is the real-space standard deviation of the blur in scan pixels. A Gaussian has no ringing and zero phase, so it does not move the peak.

  • start_template (array_like, optional) – Starting reference for "mean_template": complex (n0, n1), in the same Fourier convention as the input.

  • n_refinements (int, optional) – Number of aligned-average rebuilds (>= 0). Default 2.

  • peak_tolerance (float, optional) – In [0, 1). Peaks within this fraction of the highest peak count as equal; the one nearest to zero shift wins. This gives the true shift on a scan-periodic specimen when the shift is less than half the lattice repeat. Default 0.02.

  • remove_image_mean (bool, optional) – Remove the mean shift over all images. Default True: the absolute offset depends on the reference and carries no information.

  • status_line (bool, optional) – Show one progress line on sys.stderr. Ignored when quiet.

  • quiet (bool, optional) – No output: no log records above DEBUG, no warnings, no progress.

Returns:

Real (N, 2) on the device of the image data, in scan pixels, row i for input row i. dtype float64 for complex128 spectra, else float32: the precision follows the data. The result is the translation that registers each image onto the reference: an image equal to the reference translated by t gives −t (plus a common offset, zero after mean removal).

Return type:

Tensor

Raises:

ValueError – For an unknown shift estimator, an invalid option, spectra that are not a complex 3-D stack or source, bad coordinates, a count mismatch, a reference spectrum of the wrong shape or with "neighbour_mesh", or non-finite spectrum values.

Notes

All work runs in the canonical order of the coordinates (sorted by (q0, q1)) in blocks that depend only on the scan shape. So a permutation of the input permutes the output exactly, and the chunk size of a source never changes the result.

Degenerate inputs give, without an exception: N = 0: an empty (0, 2) tensor; N = 1: [[0, 0]] (with remove_image_mean=False and "mean_template": the shift onto the reference); all images equal: equal shifts (zero after mean removal); a constant or zero image: shift 0 relative to the reference, or dropped neighbour pairs (an isolated node gets 0); n0 = n1 = 1: zeros; one bin: every pixel gets the bin shift; a disconnected neighbour graph: zero mean per component and a WARNING record.

scatterem.reconstruction.ptychography.direct.fit_aberrations_and_rotation_to_bright_field_shifts(target_shifts: Tensor, k_sampling: ndarray | Tensor, wavelength: float, bright_field_mask: Tensor, include_in_fit_mask: Tensor | None = None, rotation_init: Tensor | None = None, rotation_requires_grad: bool = True, init_method: str = 'closed_form', residual_warn_rtol: float = 0.15, correct_order: int = 1, max_iter: int = 250, lr: float = 0.1, verbosity: int = 0) → BrightFieldShiftFit#

Fit the aberrations and rotation to the bright field shifts.

Parameters:

  • target_shifts (torch.Tensor) – Target bright-field shifts, shape (N, 2), one row per pixel of bright_field_mask in row-major (torch.argwhere) order, as aberrations_to_image_shifts(...)[bright_field_mask] lays them out.

  • k_sampling (numpy.ndarray) – Real-space sampling of the detector grid, dataset.dr (Angstrom), shape (2,) – NOT the reciprocal detector pixel size: the shift model’s frequencies are fftfreq(shape, k_sampling).

  • wavelength (float) – Electron wavelength, in Angstrom.

  • bright_field_mask (torch.Tensor) – Bright-field mask, shape (H, W).

  • include_in_fit_mask (torch.Tensor, optional) – Mask of bright-field shifts to include in the fit. Default is None, which includes all of them.

  • rotation_init (torch.Tensor, optional) – Initial rotation, in degrees. Default is None, which initializes the rotation to 0.

  • rotation_requires_grad (bool, optional) – Whether to optimize the rotation. If False the rotation is held at rotation_init (0 when None), and the closed-form seed is solved at that rotation. Default is True.

  • init_method (str, optional) – Initialization method, either “closed_form” (default: the closed-form C1, C12 and rotation estimate) or “zeros”. Either seed is then refined over the coefficients correct_order frees; “zeros” additionally caps that at order 1.

  • residual_warn_rtol (float, optional) – Relative residual limit. Above it the fit emits a UserWarning and the result’s reliable is False. The relative residual is RMS(final_shifts - target_shifts) / RMS(target_shifts). Default is 0.15.

  • correct_order (int, optional) – Highest aberration order refined: 0 is C1 only, 1 (default) C1 and C12a/b, 2 adds coma and three-fold astigmatism (C21, C23), 3 adds C30, C32 and C34. Higher-order terms correlate strongly with the low-order ones over the bright-field disk, so freeing them without such aberrations in the data biases C1 (about 6% on low-defocus data); conversely an order-1 fit absorbs a real spherical aberration into C1.

  • max_iter (int, optional) – Maximum number of LBFGS iterations. Default is 250.

  • lr (float, optional) – Learning rate. Default is 1e-1.

  • verbosity (int, optional) – Verbosity level. Default is 0.

Returns:

The fitted aberrations (Angstrom) and rotation (degrees), with the relative residual and the reliable flag. It unpacks as aberrations, rotation = fit. Check reliable before a pipeline writes the values as results; the class docstring gives the fallback order. The aberrations are in the SHIFT-MODEL frame of scatterem.utils.transfer.aberrations_to_image_shifts (the model fitted here): at rotation != 0 every m-fold pair differs from the detector-frame vector meta.aberrations holds. Convert with scatterem.utils.transfer.shift_model_to_detector_frame at the fitted rotation before using them as meta.aberrations; aberrations_and_rotation_from_bright_field_shifts() does.

Return type:

BrightFieldShiftFit

Notes

The refinement runs in float64 whatever the input dtype (outputs are float32), with LBFGS in coordinates scaled by each coefficient’s shift sensitivity, so it converges and its result does not depend on float32 rounding of the inputs.

scatterem.reconstruction.ptychography.direct.aberrations_and_rotation_from_bright_field_shifts(dataset: DatasetVirtualBrightField4DStem, fit_rotation: bool = True, target_percentage_nonzero_pixels: float = 0.75, registration_upsample_factor: int = 10, lowpass_fwhm_bright_field: float | None = None, bin_factors: tuple[int, ...] = (2, 1), verbosity: int = 0, update_dataset: bool = True, n_center_indices: int = 25, use_com_rotation_prior: str = 'auto', alignment_method: str = 'reference', init_method: str = 'closed_form', peak_selection: str = 'argmax', correct_order: int = 1) → BrightFieldShiftFit#

First determine the bright field shifts, then fit aberrations and rotation.

Parameters:

  • dataset (DatasetVirtualBrightField4DStem) – Dataset4DStem or DatasetVirtualBrightField4DStem object containing the diffraction pattern.

  • fit_rotation (bool, optional) – Whether to fit the rotation. Default is True.

  • target_percentage_nonzero_pixels (float, optional) – Target percentage of nonzero pixels for the bright field. Default is 0.75.

  • registration_upsample_factor (int, optional) – The final cross-correlation peak grid is 1 / registration_upsample_factor scan pixel (peak_grid_divisor of measure_bf_parallax()). Default is 10.

  • lowpass_fwhm_bright_field (float, optional) – FWHM of the lowpass filter for the bright field. Default is None, which applies no lowpass filter.

  • bin_factors (tuple of int, optional) – Bin factors for the bright field, applied in order. Default is (2, 1).

  • verbosity (int, optional) – Verbosity level. Default is 0.

  • update_dataset (bool, optional) – Whether to write the fitted aberrations (detector frame, as returned) and rotation back onto dataset.meta. Default is True. The write happens whether or not the fit is reliable, and a vBF shares meta with its parent dataset. To write only a reliable fit, pass False, check reliable and then write the values.

  • n_center_indices (int, optional) – Number of center indices to use for the bright field shifts. Default is 25.

  • use_com_rotation_prior (str, optional) – When “auto” (default), computes a diffraction COM-curl rotation prior and uses it as the initial rotation when meta.rotation is unset (< 1e-6 deg). An out-of-core parent dataset is measured block by block, to the same prior as its eager twin. If no pattern has a finite COM, a warning is logged and meta.rotation is kept. Set to “off” to always use meta.rotation directly.

  • alignment_method (str, optional) – “reference” (default) registers every BF image onto one common reference (shift_estimator="mean_template" of measure_bf_parallax()). “pairwise” registers detector neighbours onto each other and solves for all shifts by least squares (shift_estimator="neighbour_mesh"), which is more robust when large aberration shifts blur the reference image.

  • init_method (str, optional) – How the aberration fit is initialised, forwarded to fit_aberrations_and_rotation_to_bright_field_shifts. “closed_form” (default) seeds it with the closed-form C1, C12 and rotation estimate; “zeros” starts from zero and caps the fit at order 1. Either way the refined orders are set by correct_order.

  • peak_selection (str, optional) – Which cross-correlation peak is taken as each shift: “argmax” (default, the global maximum) or “guided” (for periodic specimens, whose correlation is multi-peaked). With “guided” and alignment_method="reference" on a periodic reference image, the images (or detector bins) are registered in order of increasing detector radius; each one takes the highest peak near a smooth prediction from the ones nearer the centre (see _peak_selection). The low-pass and the bin factors apply as for “argmax”. On a non-periodic reference image “guided” is “argmax”. With alignment_method="pairwise", “guided” takes, among the peaks within 2 % of the highest, the one nearest to zero shift. With “argmax” on a periodic specimen a UserWarning flags a likely wrong pick.

  • correct_order (int, optional) – Highest aberration order the fit refines, forwarded to fit_aberrations_and_rotation_to_bright_field_shifts. Default is 1 (C1, C12 and rotation); a real spherical aberration is then absorbed into C1 unless 3 is requested.

Returns:

The aberrations (Angstrom) and rotation (degrees) of the last bin level. The aberrations are (12,) in the DETECTOR frame of meta.aberrations (the frame the direct-ptychography kernels and tilt-corrected dark field read): the shift-model-frame fit converted with scatterem.utils.transfer.shift_model_to_detector_frame at the fitted rotation, the same as the fit at rotation == 0. relative_residual is the largest over the bin levels, and well_posed is False if any level was not well posed, so a failed earlier level makes the result not reliable. It unpacks as aberrations, rotation = fit. When reliable is False, use the fallback order in the BrightFieldShiftFit docstring.

Return type:

BrightFieldShiftFit

Raises:

ValueError – If the dataset is not a valid Dataset4DStem object, if bin_factors is empty, or if the vBF does not carry its detector sampling (a 4-entry sampling and a 2-D bright_field_mask).

Scan rotation and centre-of-mass calibration#

find_scan_rotation

Find the rotation between scan and detector from the CoM field.

ScanRotation

Result of find_scan_rotation().

Record of the angle search, for scatterem.vis.rotation_figures.angle_search_figure().

fit_origin

Fit the drift of the diffraction-space origin across the scan.

fit_2D

Fit a surface model function(xy, *coefficients) to a 2-D field.

plane

Affine surface z = mx*x + my*y + b (gradient (mx, my), offset b).

parabola

General 2-D quadratic surface, evaluated in Horner form.

Tensor-product quadratic Bezier (biquadratic Bernstein) surface.
scatterem.data.calibration.find_scan_rotation(centroid_a0, centroid_a1, *, run_device=None, quiet: bool = False, angle_grid_deg=None, fixed_angle_deg: float | None = None, fixed_axes_exchanged: bool | None = None, resolve_180: bool = True, curve_kind: str = 'curl', scan_spacing=(1.0, 1.0), keep_search: bool = False, evaluator: str = 'by_capability') → ScanRotation#

Find the rotation between scan and detector from the CoM field.

The solver evaluates the objective of rotation_objective() over the trial angles, picks the extremum (minimum for curl, maximum for divergence) and decides the handedness: the hypothesis with the better extremum wins. On an exact tie the field stays as measured, because a reflection is a strong claim that needs evidence. On exact ties within a curve the first angle in the caller’s order wins. Then the 180° test of _rotation_sign.resolve_half_turn() decides the sign.

The solver reports with logging (INFO for the decision, WARNING for an inconclusive 180° test) and with ScanReflectionWarning for a found reflection: only the caller can fix that, by a change to the data, and a warnings filter can turn it into an error. quiet=True reports nothing above DEBUG. The solver draws no figure.

Parameters:

  • centroid_a0 (Tensor or numpy.ndarray) – CoM components along axis 0 and axis 1: 2-D, real, one shape, at least 2 × 2, finite.

  • centroid_a1 (Tensor or numpy.ndarray) – CoM components along axis 0 and axis 1: 2-D, real, one shape, at least 2 × 2, finite.

  • run_device (str or torch.device, optional) – Device rule: an explicit device wins; else the device of the first tensor input; else the CPU.

  • quiet (bool, optional) – No log records above DEBUG and no warnings.

  • angle_grid_deg (array_like, optional) – Trial angles in degrees, 1-D, finite, any order. Default DEFAULT_ANGLE_GRID_DEG, [-90, 90) in steps of 0.1°: one period of the objective, with a grid error of at most 0.05°.

  • fixed_angle_deg (float, optional) – Skip the search and use this angle. The result angle is this angle wrapped into [-180, 180). No 180° test runs, and no record is returned (search is None). If fixed_axes_exchanged is None, the two hypotheses are compared at this angle.

  • fixed_axes_exchanged (bool, optional) – Fix the handedness and skip its test.

  • resolve_180 (bool, optional) – Run the 180° test. Default True: without it the angle is ambiguous by 180°, which inverts the sign of every phase downstream.

  • curve_kind ({"curl", "divergence"}, optional) – Default "curl": its target is 0 for an ideal field, so its minimum tells how good the fit is.

  • scan_spacing (float or (float, float), optional) – Scan step along axis 0 and axis 1. Only the ratio matters.

  • keep_search (bool, optional) – Also return the search record. The other outputs are bit-identical with and without it.

  • evaluator ({"by_capability", "tensor_ops"}, optional) – Implementation of the objective, see rotation_objective().

Returns:

scan_turn_deg in [-180, 180): the total rotation, including a half-turn from the 180° test. The corrected field is R(scan_turn_deg) P^h f: the half-turn is applied as an exact negation. rotated_180 flags the half-turn.

Return type:

ScanRotation

Raises:

ValueError – If the inputs are not two finite real 2-D arrays of one shape of at least 2 × 2, or an option is invalid.

class scatterem.data.calibration.ScanRotation(scan_turn_deg: float, centroid_a0: Tensor, centroid_a1: Tensor, axes_exchanged: bool, rotated_180: bool, search: RotationSearch | None)#

Result of find_scan_rotation().

Variables:

  • scan_turn_deg (float) – Total rotation applied to the (possibly swapped) field, in degrees, in the half-open interval [-180, 180). It includes the half-turn of the 180° test.

  • centroid_a1 (centroid_a0,) – The corrected field on the resolved device. dtype float64 if either input was float64, else float32.

  • axes_exchanged (bool) – True when the components were exchanged before the rotation.

  • rotated_180 (bool) – True when the 180° test added a half-turn. Then scan_turn_deg holds the half-turn and the corrected field is the negated field.

  • search (RotationSearch or None) – The search record when the caller asked for it and a search ran.

class scatterem.data.calibration.RotationSearch(curve_kind: str, angle_grid_deg: ndarray, hypothesis_curves: dict, search_angle_deg: float, scan_turn_deg: float, axes_exchanged: bool, rotated_180: bool, sign_test: str, potential_skewness: float | None, evaluator: str)#

Record of the angle search, for scatterem.vis.rotation_figures.angle_search_figure().

Variables:

  • curve_kind (str) – "curl" or "divergence".

  • angle_grid_deg (numpy.ndarray) – float64 (A,): the trial angles as given.

  • hypothesis_curves (dict of str to numpy.ndarray) – "axes_kept" and/or "axes_exchanged", float64 (A,). A hypothesis that was not evaluated has no key.

  • search_angle_deg (float) – The trial angle at the extremum of the chosen hypothesis.

  • scan_turn_deg (float) – The returned angle, equal to ScanRotation.scan_turn_deg.

  • axes_exchanged (bool) – The chosen hypothesis.

  • rotated_180 (bool) – True when the 180° test added a half-turn.

  • sign_test (str) – "kept", "flipped", "undecided" or "off".

  • potential_skewness (float or None) – Skewness of the integrated potential; None when the test did not run.

  • evaluator (str) – "tensor_ops" or "gpu_kernel".

scatterem.data.calibration.fit_origin(data: tuple[Tensor, Tensor], mask: Tensor | None = None, fit_function: str = 'plane', return_fit_params: bool = False, robust: bool = False, robust_steps: int = 3, robust_thresh: float = 2, device: str | device | None = None)#

Fit the drift of the diffraction-space origin across the scan.

The two components of the measured origin are fitted independently, each with the same smooth surface model, and the residuals returned alongside.

Parameters:

  • data ((Tensor, Tensor)) – Measured origin, as (x-component, y-component), each (Rx, Ry).

  • mask (Tensor, optional) – Boolean (Rx, Ry); scan positions where False are excluded from the fit but still get a fitted value and a residual.

  • fit_function (str) – 'constant' (per-component mean) or one of the keys of _ORIGIN_SURFACES.

  • return_fit_params (bool) – Also return the coefficients and covariances of the two fits. They are None for fit_function='constant', which has no fitted model.

  • robust – Outlier rejection, forwarded to fit_2D().

  • robust_steps – Outlier rejection, forwarded to fit_2D().

  • robust_thresh – Outlier rejection, forwarded to fit_2D().

  • device (str, torch.device or None) – Default: the device of data[0] if it is a tensor, else CPU.

Returns:

Each (Rx, Ry). If return_fit_params, a 2-tuple of that and (popt_x, popt_y, pcov_x, pcov_y).

Return type:

(qx0_fit, qy0_fit, qx0_residuals, qy0_residuals)

Notes

Clean-room implementation from a behavioural specification, with the interface kept from py4DSTEM, except that fit_function and return_fit_params are new spellings of fitfunction and returnfitp (see _surfaces). The method is that of Savitzky et al. (2021) and Ophus (2019): the descan is a slow, smooth drift, so a low-order surface fitted to each component removes it and leaves the specimen signal in the residual.

scatterem.data.calibration.fit_2D(function, data: Tensor, data_mask: Tensor | None = None, popt=None, robust: bool = False, robust_steps: int = 3, robust_thresh: float = 2, device: str | device | None = None, need_pcov: bool = True)#

Fit a surface model function(xy, *coefficients) to a 2-D field.

The field is sampled on the unit square (_make_xy_flat()). The three models of this module are solved in closed form by linear least squares; any other callable is fitted by L-BFGS from popt. Clean-room implementation from a behavioural specification, with the interface kept from py4DSTEM (see the module docstring); method of Savitzky et al. (2021) and Ophus (2019).

Parameters:

  • function (callable) – Model whose first argument is the (2, N) coordinates and whose other arguments are the P coefficients.

  • data (Tensor (H, W)) – Field to fit; it is read as float32 and fitted in float64.

  • data_mask (Tensor (H, W), optional) – Boolean; only points where it is True enter the fit. Default: all.

  • popt (sequence or Tensor, optional) – Initial coefficients, P of them. Default: zeros. Used only by the L-BFGS path.

  • robust (bool) – Re-fit robust_steps more times, each time removing from the mask the points whose squared residual is larger than robust_thresh**2 times the mean squared residual over the whole field.

  • robust_steps (int)

  • robust_thresh (float)

  • device (str, torch.device or None) – Default: the device of data if it is a tensor, else CPU.

  • need_pcov (bool) – False skips the parameter covariance of a linear basis and returns the NaN placeholder in its slot; everything else is unchanged. Default True.

Returns:

  • popt (Tensor (P,), float64)

  • pcov (Tensor (P, P), float64)

  • fit (Tensor (H, W), float32)

  • mask (Tensor (H, W), bool) – The points used by the last fit.

scatterem.data.calibration.plane(xy, mx, my, b)#

Affine surface z = mx*x + my*y + b (gradient (mx, my), offset b).

scatterem.data.calibration.parabola(xy, c0, cx1, cx2, cy1, cy2, cxy)#

General 2-D quadratic surface, evaluated in Horner form.

z = c0 + cx1*x + cx2*x^2 + cy1*y + cy2*y^2 + cxy*x*y – the complete second-order polynomial in two variables, grouped as c0 + x*(cx1 + cx2*x + cxy*y) + y*(cy1 + cy2*y) so each variable is touched once.

scatterem.data.calibration.bezier_two(xy, c00, c01, c02, c10, c11, c12, c20, c21, c22)#

Tensor-product quadratic Bezier (biquadratic Bernstein) surface.

z = sum_{i,j} c_ij * B_i(x) * B_j(y) over the degree-2 Bernstein basis of _bernstein_quadratic(), i.e. a 3x3 grid of control values c_ij with i indexing x and j indexing y. Because the basis is a partition of unity the surface interpolates the corner coefficients (c00 at (0,0), c22 at (1,1)) and stays within the convex hull of all nine.

Scan-rotation figures#

angle_search_figure

Plot the objective curves of a scan-rotation search.

plot_scan_maps

Show 2-D scan maps in physical scan coordinates.
scatterem.vis.rotation_figures.angle_search_figure(search: RotationSearch, *, figure_inches=(5.0, 3.2)) → Figure#

Plot the objective curves of a scan-rotation search.

Layout: one axes, one line per evaluated hypothesis against the trial angle (sorted by angle for drawing; the record is not changed). Colours are the first two colours of the categorical role "labels"; line styles are solid for “as measured” and dashed for “components swapped (reflection)”, so the hypotheses stay apart without colour vision too. Each legend label ends with the extremum of its curve. A dotted dark-grey vertical line marks search_angle_deg: that line lies in the plotted range, and its label gives the final angle when the 180° test added a half-turn. NaN and ±inf values are drawn as gaps; a constant curve is a flat line; if no value is finite, the axes say so. No case raises.

Parameters:

  • search (RotationSearch) – The record from find_scan_rotation(..., keep_search=True).

  • figure_inches ((float, float), optional) – Figure size in inches. Default (5.0, 3.2).

Returns:

A new open figure with one axes.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure

Raises:

ValueError – If search is not a RotationSearch.

scatterem.vis.rotation_figures.plot_scan_maps(scan_images: Sequence, *, scan_spacing, distance_unit, map_captions: Sequence[str] | None = None, panel_grid: tuple[int, int] | None = None, figure_inches: tuple[float, float] | None = None, colour_role=None, colour_map=None, limits=None, colour_key: bool = True, length_bar: bool = True) → Figure#

Show 2-D scan maps in physical scan coordinates.

Geometry: each map is drawn as stored, rows (axis 0, “x”) vertical and columns (axis 1, “y”) horizontal, origin="upper". Pixel centres sit at k · step, so the axes span n · step along each axis, with equal aspect in data units. Colour: by default a map with any finite value below zero takes the diverging role "signed" with limits symmetric about 0, so the neutral colour sits at zero; other maps take "intensity". NaN shows in the NaN colour of the policy. Each panel has a horizontal scale bar along axis 1, its title and (by default) a colour bar.

Parameters:

  • scan_images (sequence of Tensor or numpy.ndarray) – Real 2-D maps; shapes may differ. Tensors may be on any device.

  • scan_spacing (float or (float, float)) – Step between scan positions along axis 0 and axis 1. Required: a silent default would hide a missing calibration.

  • distance_unit (str or (str, str)) – Length unit per axis; "A" prints as “Å”. Required.

  • map_captions (sequence of str, optional) – One per map. Default "map 0", "map 1", …

  • panel_grid ((int, int), optional) – (rows, cols). Default cols = ceil(sqrt(n)), rows = ceil(n / cols). Unused panels are removed.

  • figure_inches ((float, float), optional) – Override. Default (3.4 · cols, 3.0 · rows) inches.

  • colour_role (str or sequence of str, optional) – Override of the automatic colour role, one for all or one per map.

  • colour_map (str or Colormap, optional) – Override with an explicit map (an unscientific map warns).

  • limits ((float, float) or sequence of them, optional) – Override of the display limits (vmin, vmax), one for all or one per map.

  • colour_key (bool, optional) – Draw a colour bar per panel. Default True.

  • length_bar (bool, optional) – Draw a scale bar per panel. Default True.

Returns:

A new open figure with one image panel per map.

Return type:

matplotlib.figure.Figure

Raises:

ValueError – For an empty map list, a map that is not real 2-D, a bad step or unit, a wrong count of captions, roles or limits, or a panel grid that does not fit the maps.

Return type:

scatterem.reconstruction.darkfield.tilt_corrected_dark_field_depth_section(dataset: Dataset4DStem, depth_angstroms=<built-in method tensor of type object>, bright_field_mask_threshold: float = 0.3, return_device: device | None = None, upsample: float | str = 'nyquist', n_dark_field_segments: int = 32, verbosity: int = 0, dark_field_scaling: bool = False, dead_frame_fraction: float = 0.001, region: str = 'dark_field', return_snr: bool = False, ssnr_return_device: device | None = None, _segment_geometry: _SegmentGeometry | None = None) → Tensor | tuple[Tensor, Tensor | None]#

Stack tcDF reconstructions swept over a defocus (depth) series.

Runs tilt_corrected_dark_field() once per entry of depth_angstroms (each added to aberrations[0]) and stacks the results as (n_depths, ny * up, nx * up), with up the one isotropic factor tilt_corrected_dark_field() uses (the larger of the two per-axis factors upsample resolves to). dark_field_scaling / dead_frame_fraction / region are those of tilt_corrected_dark_field() and are shared by all depths: the segment geometry that carries them is built once. The probe has the aberrations meta.aberrations with C10 less meta.defocus_guess, as in direct_ptychography().

Parameters:

  • dataset (Dataset4DStem) – The 4D-STEM dataset to reconstruct from.

  • depth_angstroms (torch.Tensor) – Defocus offsets, in Angstrom, added to aberrations[0] at each step. The guess meta.defocus_guess is subtracted once.

  • bright_field_mask_threshold (float, optional) – Fraction of the peak mean-CBED intensity above which a detector pixel is classified as bright field.

  • return_device (torch.device, optional) – Device the returned stack is placed on. Defaults to CPU.

  • upsample (float or str, optional) – Upsampling factor applied to the reconstructed grid, or "nyquist" to resolve it from the acquisition geometry. On an anisotropic scan, "nyquist" resolves to two factors, and the larger one applies to both axes.

  • n_dark_field_segments (int, optional) – Number of azimuthal detector segments.

  • verbosity (int, optional) – Diagnostic-plot verbosity, forwarded to tilt_corrected_dark_field().

  • dark_field_scaling (bool, optional) – Rescale each segment image to account for scattering past the detector edge.

  • dead_frame_fraction (float, optional) – Minimum fraction of the incident current a scan position must record to receive dark_field_scaling correction.

  • region ({"dark_field", "bright_field"}, optional) – Which detector pixels feed the azimuthal segments.

  • return_snr (bool, optional) – Also return the per-plane half-set SSNR stack – a by-product of the two half-set images tilt_corrected_dark_field() builds either way. With the default False the return is the bare image stack, unchanged.

  • ssnr_return_device (torch.device, optional) – Device the SSNR stack is placed on. Defaults to return_device, so a fusion that consumes the SSNR on the GPU can keep it resident while the image cube goes to the host.

  • _segment_geometry (_SegmentGeometry, optional) – Precomputed segment geometry, built on dataset with these parameters. Private. Default builds it.

Returns:

The stacked tcDF images, shape (n_depths, ny * up, nx * up), on return_device. With return_snr=True, that stack and the per-plane half-set SSNR stack on ssnr_return_device; the SSNR slot is None only when depth_angstroms is empty (no plane to size it by).

Return type:

torch.Tensor or tuple of torch.Tensor

  • provenance (Provenance) – Where the result came from; its config has the threshold and the segment count resolved.

  • diagnostics (Mapping, optional) – {"vbf_cache": ...} when a vBF cache was passed in, else empty.

  • fused (torch.Tensor) – The fused image, on the upsampled grid, on the dataset’s device.

  • phase_weighted (torch.Tensor or None) – The low-frequency channel after its weight (None unless the fusion’s verbosity fills it, as in the function).

  • tcdf_weighted (torch.Tensor or None) – The dark-field channel after its weight (likewise).

  • phase_image (torch.Tensor) – The low-frequency image that was fused: the SSB phase, or the negated, mean-subtracted tilt-corrected bright field.

  • ptycho (Result) – The low-frequency channel’s own result (a DirectPtychographyResult, or a TiltCorrectedDarkFieldResult with region="bright_field").

  • tcdf (TiltCorrectedDarkFieldResult) – The dark-field channel’s result.

  • sampling (Sampling) – The pixel size (dy, dx) of fused and its units, the scan step divided by the upsample factor (from reconstruction_sampling()). Pass it to vis.show_2d(..., sampling=) or diagnostics.metrics.frc(..., pixel_size=).

as_tuple() → tuple[Tensor, Tensor | None, Tensor | None]#

Return (fused, phase_weighted, tcdf_weighted).

The three images of the result, in this order.
