class scatterem.physics.periodic_sampling.PeriodicGrid(points: tuple[int, ...], lengths: tuple[float, ...])#

A periodic sampling grid: point counts and periods per axis.

Parameters:

  • points (tuple of int) – Number of samples N_i per axis, axis order (..., y, x).

  • lengths (tuple of float) – Period L_i of each axis [Angstrom].

Raises:

ValueError – If the tuples differ in length, are empty, if a count is not an integer of at least 1, or if a period is not finite and positive.

Notes

The grid stores the period, not the pixel size. One IEEE division of the exact integer j by L then gives the correctly rounded j / L. The object is hashable.

classmethod from_pixel_sizes(points, pixel_sizes) → PeriodicGrid#

Make a grid from point counts and pixel sizes.

Parameters:

  • points (sequence of int) – Number of samples per axis.

  • pixel_sizes (sequence of float) – Sample spacing per axis [Angstrom].

Returns:

The grid with L_i = N_i * d_i, rounded once. The stored L_i is the reference for all frequencies.

Return type:

PeriodicGrid

scatterem.physics.periodic_sampling.dft_sample_frequencies(grid: PeriodicGrid) → tuple[ndarray, ...]#

Return the spatial frequencies that the DFT samples on a grid.

On an axis with N points and period L [Angstrom], the DFT samples the spectrum at j / L for the FFT-order integers j: 0, 1, ..., (N - 1) // 2 and then -(N // 2), ..., -1 (Press et al. 2007, sec. 12.1).

Parameters:

grid (PeriodicGrid) – The grid.

Returns:

One float64 array per axis [1/Angstrom]. The array of axis i has length N_i on axis i and length 1 on all other axes, so the arrays broadcast to the full grid. np.broadcast_arrays gives full views without a copy. Each value is one IEEE division of an exact integer and is correctly rounded. The arrays are new on each call.

Return type:

tuple of numpy.ndarray

class scatterem.physics.periodic_sampling.CircularPassBand(band_grid: PeriodicGrid, cut_fraction: float, rim_samples: float = 2.0)#

Isotropic pass band in physical frequency on a 2-D grid.

The cut radius is k_c = cut_fraction * min(N_y / (2 L_y), N_x / (2 L_x)) [1/Angstrom]. The rim width is w = rim_samples * max(1 / L_y, 1 / L_x) [1/Angstrom], and the flat radius is k_f = k_c - w. With |k|^2 = (j_y / L_y)**2 + (j_x / L_x)**2 (float64), the mask is 1 for |k| <= k_f, 0 for |k| >= k_c and sin(pi/2 * (k_c - |k|) / w)**2 on the rim. The rim is the Hann taper (Harris 1978). In exact arithmetic rim values are strictly between 0 and 1. A rim point within rounding of k_f or k_c can round to 1 or 0.

Parameters:

  • band_grid (PeriodicGrid) – A 2-D grid (y, x). Pixel sizes can differ.

  • cut_fraction (float) – k_c as a fraction of the lower Nyquist frequency [dimensionless], in (0, 1]. The argument is required. A value of at most 1 keeps the circle inside the Nyquist rectangle. A value of at most 2/3 makes a product of two band-limited fields alias-free on both axes (see ellipse_mask()).

  • rim_samples (float, optional) – Rim width in frequency steps of the coarser axis [dimensionless], greater than 0. The default 2 is the smallest width that puts at least one sample strictly on the rim on each axis. A wider rim gives less ringing and a smaller flat band.

Raises:

ValueError – If the grid is not 2-D, if a parameter is out of range, or if k_f < 0.

Notes

Keep one object for one multislice run. The transmission step and the propagation step then use identical pass bands. The object has no mutable state, and equal inputs give equal masks.

mask(*, device: device | str | None = None, dtype: dtype | None = None) → Tensor#

Return the pass-band mask.

Parameters:

  • device (torch.device or str, optional) – Device. Default: the CPU.

  • dtype (torch.dtype, optional) – Real floating dtype. Default: the torch default dtype.

Returns:

Real mask (Ny, Nx) in FFT order, values in [0, 1]. The caller owns the tensor. A float32 mask is the float64 mask rounded once.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

min_crop_shape() → tuple[int, int]#

Return the smallest lossless centred crop box (M_y, M_x).

The centred crop of M points keeps j from -(M // 2) to M - 1 - M // 2. Padding back returns every kept value to its own frequency. With J_i the largest |j_i| where the float64 mask is not zero, the smallest box is M_i = 2 J_i + 1, never above N_i. A mask of lower precision has no more non-zero points, so the box is valid for every dtype.

Returns:

(M_y, M_x) [samples].

Return type:

tuple of int

scatterem.physics.periodic_sampling.apply_pass_band(field: Tensor, mask: Tensor) → Tensor#

Return the band-limited real-space field ifft2(fft2(field) * mask).

Parameters:

  • field (torch.Tensor) – Complex field (..., Ny, Nx) in real space.

  • mask (torch.Tensor) – Real mask (Ny, Nx) in FFT order, for example from CircularPassBand.mask(). The function moves it to the device and real dtype of field.

Returns:

New field with the shape and dtype of field. Neither input changes; the autograd graph of field stays intact. A complex32 field is computed in complex64 and cast back, so the FFT sum cannot overflow.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

Raises:

  • TypeError – If field is not complex.

  • ValueError – If the mask shape does not match the last two axes of field.

  • OverflowError – If a complex32 result has a part above the float16 range.

scatterem.physics.periodic_sampling.ellipse_mask(shape: tuple[int, int], nyquist_fraction: float | tuple[float, float], *, half_last_axis: bool, fade_depth: float = 0.0, device: device | str | None = None, dtype: dtype | None = None) → Tensor#

Return a low-pass mask that keeps the frequencies inside an ellipse.

The ellipse is centred on zero frequency, with its axes on the grid axes. Its semi-axis on axis i is rho_i times the Nyquist frequency. In index units it is R_i = rho_i N_i / 2. For the FFT integers (j_y, j_x) the code computes, in float64:

num = (j_y R_x)**2 + (j_x R_y)**2,   den = (R_y R_x)**2

The normalised radius is r = sqrt(num / den). A point is inside if num < den. A point with num >= den (r >= 1, also r exactly 1) gets the value 0. For R_i integer or half-integer below about 2**20 this test is exact.

Alias-free size: let two fields have spectra in the open ellipse E. Their product has its spectrum in E + E = 2E. The DFT wraps frequency j onto j + (m_y N_y, m_x N_x) with integer m. A wrapped copy reaches E only if the shift lies in 2E - E = 3E. The shortest shifts are along one axis, with normalised length N_i / R_i. So no copy reaches E if N_i / R_i >= 3 on both axes, that is rho_i <= 2/3. Boundary points are removed, so equality is safe. This is the 2/3 rule of Kirkland (2010, sec. 6.8).

Smooth edge: with depth t = 1 - r and w = fade_depth > 0, the value is 0 for num >= den, 1 for t >= w, and sin(pi/2 * t / w)**2 between. This is the Hann taper (Harris 1978). It is monotone in t, has a continuous slope at both ends and stays inside the cut, so the alias-free result stays true.

Parameters:

  • shape (tuple of int) – Full grid shape (Ny, Nx), also for the half layout.

  • nyquist_fraction (float or tuple of float) – rho [dimensionless], one value for both axes or (rho_y, rho_x), each in (0, 1]. The argument is required. The value 2/3 is the largest alias-free value; its float64 value is a little below 2/3.

  • half_last_axis (bool) – Required. If True, return the torch.fft.rfft2 layout (Ny, Nx // 2 + 1); column n holds j_x = n. If False, return the full layout (Ny, Nx).

  • fade_depth (float, optional) – Depth w of the smooth edge [normalised radius], in [0, 1). The default 0 gives the hard edge: it keeps the full alias-free band and filtering twice equals filtering once.

  • device (torch.device or str, optional) – Device of the result. Default: the CPU.

  • dtype (torch.dtype, optional) – Real floating dtype of the result. Default: the torch default dtype.

Returns:

Real mask (Ny, Nx) in FFT order, values in [0, 1]. The caller owns the tensor and can change it.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

Raises:

  • ValueError – If shape, nyquist_fraction or fade_depth is out of range.

  • TypeError – If dtype is not a real floating dtype.

Notes

The code builds the mask once in float64 on the CPU and keeps the result of each dtype and device in a bounded LRU store (32 masks, 256 MiB). A repeat request returns a clone of the stored mask. A float32 mask is the float64 mask rounded once, so the two agree to 0.5 float32 ulp at every point. The brief allows differences for points within float32 rounding of the cut or of the inner end of the edge; this design has none. CPU and CUDA masks are equal bit for bit.

scatterem.physics.periodic_sampling.lowpass_ellipse(field: Tensor, nyquist_fraction: float | tuple[float, float], *, fade_depth: float = 0.0) → Tensor#

Return a complex real-space field band-limited by the ellipse mask.

The function computes ifft2(fft2(field) * mask) with the mask of ellipse_mask() for the shape, real dtype and device of field. The arguments and their reasons are those of ellipse_mask().

Parameters:

  • field (torch.Tensor) – Complex field (..., Ny, Nx) in real space. The mask broadcasts over the leading axes.

  • nyquist_fraction (float or tuple of float) – Semi-axes as fractions of the Nyquist frequency [dimensionless]. Required; 2/3 is the largest alias-free value.

  • fade_depth (float, optional) – Depth of the smooth edge [normalised radius]; 0 is the hard edge.

Returns:

New complex field with the shape and dtype of field. The input does not change, and the autograd graph stays intact.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

Raises:

TypeError – If field is not complex.

STEM-EELS and PRISM driver#

PrismEelsSimulator

Core-loss EELS and elastic CBED of a periodic cell with PRISM kernels.

PrismResult

The output of one PrismEelsSimulator call.
class scatterem.simulation.eels.PrismEelsSimulator(structure: AtomSet, *, eV: float, semiconvergence_angle: float, pixels: Sequence[int], scan: Sequence[int], num_slices: int = 1, defocus: float = 0.0, interpolation_factor: int = 1, num_frozen_phonons: int = 1, displacements: bool = False, seed: int | None = None, device: str | device | None = None, dtype: dtype = torch.complex64)#

Core-loss EELS and elastic CBED of a periodic cell with PRISM kernels.

The grid is the whole cell: pixels samples structure.sides[:2]. The scan is a regular raster of scan positions over the cell, half a step from its edges. An ionized site contributes with the weight that its atom has in the elastic potential: its site_fraction when the structure has a partial occupancy, else 1. A site with fraction 0 does not ionize.

Parameters:

  • structure (AtomSet) – Rectangular box and atoms (fractional (y, x, depth) and Z).

  • eV (float) – Probe energy [eV].

  • semiconvergence_angle (float) – Probe-forming aperture semi-angle [mrad].

  • pixels (sequence of int) – Real-space grid (Ny, Nx) across the cell.

  • scan (sequence of int) – Number of scan positions (Sy, Sx).

  • num_slices (int, optional) – Number of equal slices of the cell along the beam. Default 1.

  • defocus (float, optional) – Probe defocus [Angstrom]; the aperture carries exp(-i pi lambda defocus |q|^2). Default 0.

  • interpolation_factor (int, optional) – PRISM interpolation factor f (Ophus 2017) of every output. Default 1 keeps every aperture beam.

  • num_frozen_phonons (int, optional) – Number of specimen configurations averaged. Default 1.

  • displacements (bool, optional) – Draw thermal displacements for each configuration. Default False. In each EELS configuration the ionized atoms move with their atoms in the elastic potential (one draw for both).

  • seed (int or None, optional) – Draw seed of configuration 0; configuration c uses ThermalJitter(draw_seed=seed + c). Default None: each configuration takes a fresh seed, which ThermalJitter logs at INFO.

  • device (str or torch.device or None, optional) – Device of every tensor. None (default): the CPU, the device of the NumPy AtomSet (simulator convention). Pass "cuda" for the GPU.

  • dtype (torch.dtype, optional) – torch.complex64 (default) or torch.complex128 for the EELS kernels. The elastic CBED runs in the precision of PrismScanOp.

Variables:

  • sampling (wavelength, gridsize,) – Electron wavelength [Angstrom]; cell size sides[:2] and pixel size gridsize / pixels [Angstrom].

  • slice_distance (slice_thickness,) – sides[2] / num_slices, and the propagation distance the EELS kernels take: slice_thickness, but 0.0 for one slice.

  • device (torch.device) – The resolved device. Every other argument is stored under its name.

Raises:

ValueError – If dtype is not complex64 or complex128, or a count is below 1.

The probe uses the aperture of probe_q() on the PRISM window pixels // interpolation_factor and carries unit total intensity.

  • focal_backprop (float or str, optional) – Reference plane of the partitioned interpolation, passed to PrismScanOp. Default "centroid". Ignored without n_radial.

class scatterem.simulation.eels.PrismResult(data: Tensor, output: Literal['map', 'qeels', 'cube', 'cbed'], energy: float, detector_sampling: tuple[float, float], edge: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None, epsilon: float | None = None, energy_losses: ndarray | None = None, q_pixels: Tensor | None = None)#

The output of one PrismEelsSimulator call.

Parameters:

  • data (torch.Tensor) –

    Real, non-negative intensities, averaged over the frozen-phonon configurations. The shape depends on output:

    • "map": scan;

    • "qeels": scan + (n_q,), one bin per entry of q_pixels;

    • "cube": scan + pixels, corner-origin diffraction patterns;

    • "cbed": scan + window, corner-origin diffraction patterns on the PRISM window pixels // interpolation_factor.

  • output ({"map", "qeels", "cube", "cbed"}) – What data holds.

  • energy (float) – Probe energy [eV].

  • detector_sampling (tuple of float) – Reciprocal pixel (dky, dkx) of the diffraction axes of data [1/Angstrom]. For "qeels" it converts q_pixels to 1/Angstrom.

  • edge (tuple of int or None, optional) – (Z, n, l) of the ionized subshell; None for "cbed".

  • epsilon (float or None, optional) – Energy of the ejected electron above the threshold [eV]; None for "cbed".

  • energy_losses (numpy.ndarray or None, optional) – Energy loss of each summed transition [eV]; None for "cbed".

  • q_pixels (torch.Tensor or None, optional) – For "qeels": the detector coordinates that prism_eels_image returns with the patterns, in grid pixels. (n_q, 2) in (qy, qx) order for qeels_axis="both", (n_q,) for a one-axis projection. None for the other outputs.

Transition potentials#

subshell_transitions

All channels of one ionised subshell at one continuum energy.

build_transition_potentials

Real-space transition potentials H_n0 on a periodic grid.

Transition

One ionisation channel: bound orbital (l, ml) to continuum (l', ml').

TransitionPotentials

Real-space transition potentials of a set of channels on one grid.

AtomicRadialWavefunction

Radial one-electron state u(r) = r R(r) on a grid in Bohr.

bound_wavefunction

Bound radial state (n, l) of element Z, cached on disk.

continuum_wavefunction

Continuum radial state l' at epsilon eV above threshold, cached.

gpaw_available

Tell if gpaw can be imported, without importing it.

cache_dir

Return the EELS on-disk cache directory and create it if it is missing.

HydrogenicFallbackWarning

wavefunctions="auto" fell back to the analytic hydrogenic family.
scatterem.simulation.eels.subshell_transitions(Z: int, n: int, l: int, epsilon: float, lprimes: Sequence[int] | None = None, order: int = 1, wavefunctions: str = 'auto', xc: str = 'PBE', potential_scale: float = 1.0) → list[Transition]#

All channels of one ionised subshell at one continuum energy.

Parameters:

  • Z (int) – Element and the ionized bound orbital (e.g. Fe L edge: Z=26, n=2, l=1).

  • n (int) – Element and the ionized bound orbital (e.g. Fe L edge: Z=26, n=2, l=1).

  • l (int) – Element and the ionized bound orbital (e.g. Fe L edge: Z=26, n=2, l=1).

  • epsilon (float) – Energy of the ejected electron above the ionization threshold [eV]. Selecting different epsilon selects different points along the energy-loss edge.

  • lprimes (list of int, optional) – Continuum angular momenta to include. Default: every l' >= 0 with |l - l'| <= order.

  • order (int) – Maximum change in angular momentum |l - l'| retained when lprimes is not given explicitly. The leading small-K term of a channel has the multipole order |l - l'|, so order = 1 keeps the dipole channels and the l' = l channel.

  • wavefunctions (str) – "auto" (default: GPAW if importable, else hydrogenic with a HydrogenicFallbackWarning), "gpaw" or "hydrogenic". "auto" resolves once per call, so the fallback warns once.

  • xc (str) – Exchange-correlation functional for the GPAW wavefunctions.

  • potential_scale (float) – Multiplier on the atomic potential of the GPAW continuum states.

Returns:

One entry per (l', ml, mlprime) combination, ordered by l', then ml, then mlprime.

Return type:

list of Transition

scatterem.simulation.eels.build_transition_potentials(transitions: Sequence[Transition], Z: int, gpts: Sequence[int], sampling: Sequence[float], eV: float, bandlimit: float | None = 0.6666666666666666, device=None, dtype: dtype = torch.complex64, method: str = 'auto') → TransitionPotentials#

Real-space transition potentials H_n0 on a periodic grid.

fft2(array) = H~(2 pi f) / (dy dx) inside the band limit, with H~ = sigma(E0) sqrt(2 k_0/k_n) 4 pi (E_h a_0) epsilon_eV(K) / |K|^2 (see the module docstring for the frame, phase, spin factor and units). The origin is the corner pixel. The forward models use psi_n = H_n0 psi_0.

Parameters:

  • transitions (list of Transition) – Channels from subshell_transitions().

  • Z (int) – Atomic number of the ionized element.

  • gpts (int) – Shape (2,). Grid size (Ny, Nx).

  • sampling (float) – Shape (2,). Real-space pixel size (dy, dx) [Å].

  • eV (float) – Probe energy [eV].

  • bandlimit (float or None) – Radius of the hard elliptical band limit in reciprocal space, as a fraction of the Nyquist frequency of each axis. Default 2/3. None applies no band limit.

  • device (torch.device, optional) – Device of the returned array. Default None: the CPU.

  • dtype (torch.dtype) – Complex dtype of the returned array.

  • method (str) – One of "auto", "gpu" or "cpu". Backend for the partial- wave / radial-overlap / form-factor build. "auto" (default) runs the vectorised path on device, or with device=None on CUDA when available, else on the CPU; "gpu" forces CUDA; "cpu" numpy.

Returns:

Real-space transition potentials on the requested grid, in eV^(-1/2).

Return type:

TransitionPotentials

class scatterem.simulation.eels.AtomicRadialWavefunction(n: int | None, l: int, energy: float, r: ndarray, u: ndarray)#

Radial one-electron state u(r) = r R(r) on a grid in Bohr.

Parameters:

  • n (int | None) – Principal and orbital angular-momentum quantum numbers. n is None for continuum states.

  • l (int | None) – Principal and orbital angular-momentum quantum numbers. n is None for continuum states.

  • energy (float) – Orbital energy in eV. Negative for bound states, positive (energy above the ionization threshold) for continuum states.

  • r (ndarray) – Radial grid in Bohr, strictly ascending.

  • u (ndarray) – u(r) = r * R(r) sampled on r.

wavefunctions="auto" fell back to the analytic hydrogenic family.

GPAW is not importable, so the bound and continuum states are the analytic approximations. Cross-sections and EELS images then differ from the GPAW results and are not quantitative.

scatterem.simulation.eels.multislice_transition_potential(probes: Tensor, transmissions: Tensor, transition_potentials: TransitionPotentials, sites: ndarray, *, wavelength: float, gridsize: Sequence[float], slice_distance: float, site_threshold: float = 0.0, batch_size: int | None = None, return_real_space: bool = False) → Tensor#

Energy-filtered diffraction patterns for a batch of probe positions.

Parameters:

  • probes (Tensor) – Complex real-space probes (P, Ny, Nx) already placed at their scan positions.

  • transmissions (Tensor) – Complex real-space transmission functions (NZ, Ny, Nx) – one per depth slice.

  • transition_potentials (TransitionPotentials) – Real-space transition potentials for the chosen edge.

  • sites (ndarray) – Fractional coordinates (Nsite, 3) (y, x, z) in [0, 1) of the ionizable atoms (element transition_potentials.Z) within the field of view.

  • wavelength (float) – Probe wavelength [Å].

  • gridsize (float) – Shape (2,). Field-of-view size (Ly, Lx) [Å].

  • slice_distance (float) – Inter-slice propagation distance Δz [Å].

  • site_threshold (float) – Skip a site when, for every probe of the batch and every transition, the probe intensity that the site sees (the |H|^2-weighted mean of |psi|^2) is below this value. The unit is the intensity of a unit-amplitude plane wave. The module docstring gives the derivation and the error bound. The default 0 skips nothing.

  • batch_size (int, optional) – Probe-position batch size (memory control). Defaults to all probes.

  • return_real_space (bool) – If True, return the accumulated real-space exit intensity instead of the diffraction-space intensity.

Returns:

Real, non-negative intensity (P, Ny, Nx) – the inelastically scattered diffraction pattern (corner origin) summed over all transitions and sites, per incident electron and per eV of energy loss: |fft2|^2 / (Ny Nx), or |psi|^2 with return_real_space.

Return type:

Tensor

scatterem.simulation.eels.prism_transition_potential(probe_q: Tensor, transmissions: Tensor, transition_potentials: TransitionPotentials, sites: ndarray, scan_pixels: Tensor, *, wavelength: float, gridsize: Sequence[float], slice_distance: float, return_real_space: bool = False, interpolation_factor=1, partition=None, scan_chunk: int | None = None) → Tensor#

Dual-scattering-matrix PRISM STEM-EELS (Brown & Ophus).

Implements the two-scattering-matrix algorithm of Brown, Ciston & Ophus, Phys. Rev. Research 1, 033186 (2019), Eq. (11):

S_{n,iz} = S2 . F . H_{n0} . F^{-1} . S1,

where \(\mathcal S_1\) propagates the probe-forming plane waves from the entrance surface to the ionization slice iz and \(\mathcal S_2\) propagates the inelastically-scattered wave from iz to the exit surface.

The key to the full PRISM benefit (vs. prism_transition_potential_hybrid()) is the order of operations. Because every operator after \(\mathcal S_1\) is linear, the exit wave for scan position p is:

psi_exit(p) = S2[ H_n0 . (sum_b coeff_p[b] S1_col[b]) ]
            = sum_b coeff_p[b] * S2[ H_n0 . S1_col[b] ],

so the transition is applied to the Nbeams columns of \(\mathcal S_1\) and those columns are propagated to the exit (the action of \(\mathcal S_2\)), then the scan positions are synthesised by the same linear combination used to form the probe. The expensive exit-surface multislice therefore runs Nbeams times per (site, transition) – independent of the number of scan positions P – instead of P times. For P >> Nbeams (a dense scan through a small aperture, the PRISM regime) this is the source of the near-linear scaling.

With the exact per-pixel scattering matrix (partition=None) the result is identical (to float rounding) to prism_transition_potential_hybrid(); this routine just reorders the work. Energy-filtered 4D output is preserved – S2 is applied as on-the-fly multislice of the column basis (the full exit diffraction pattern is kept, so no detector reduction is made). Detector-integrating the returned cube over an EELS aperture reproduces the Brown & Ophus I(x, y) image.

Shrinking the column count (two compatible levers).

  • interpolation_factor = f subsamples the aperture beams to Nbeams / f**2 columns – exact within the PRISM aliasing window – shrinking the exact columns of both legs (S1 build and exit) by f**2.

  • partition (e.g. {"n_radial": 4}) builds S1 on Bp << Nbeams parent beams (Pelz/Ophus partitioned PRISM), then reconstructs the exact aperture columns from the parents at the ionization plane and runs the same dual-S exit. This cheapens the S1 build + memory (Bp parent propagations) and is approximate (natural-neighbor reconstruction error – accurate in-focus / thin / small-aperture, degrading with thickness/aperture); the exit leg still propagates the reconstructed Nbeams / f**2 columns, so the dual-S P-independence is preserved. Note partitioning does not reduce the (usually dominant) exit leg – only the S1 build; interpolation_factor is the lever for the exit. The two compose (partition partitions the already-subsampled aperture). Unlike partitioning S2, this is correct: the reconstruction resolves the position-dependent NNW basis before H_{n0} is applied (see PartitionedScatteringMatrix.reconstruct_columns).

Parameters:

  • probe_q – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • transmissions – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • transition_potentials – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • sites – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • scan_pixels – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • wavelength – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • gridsize – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • slice_distance – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • return_real_space – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • interpolation_factor – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • partition – As in prism_transition_potential_hybrid(). partition and interpolation_factor may be combined.

  • scan_chunk (int, optional) – Number of scan positions synthesised per batch (caps the (scan_chunk, Ny, Nx) temporary in the linear-combination step). None (the default) sizes the batch by a byte budget instead of a row count – see _SCAN_CHUNK_BUDGET_B. An explicit value is honoured exactly.

Returns:

Intensity (P, Ny, Nx) summed over transitions and sites, per incident electron and per eV of energy loss: |fft2|^2 / (Ny Nx), or |psi|^2 with return_real_space.

Return type:

Tensor

scatterem.simulation.eels.prism_transition_potential_hybrid(probe_q: Tensor, transmissions: Tensor, transition_potentials: TransitionPotentials, sites: ndarray, scan_pixels: Tensor, *, wavelength: float, gridsize: Sequence[float], slice_distance: float, return_real_space: bool = False, interpolation_factor=1, partition=None) → Tensor#

Hybrid PRISM/multislice STEM-EELS (single scattering matrix).

This is the original implementation: the first scattering matrix \(\mathcal S_1\) (reused across scan positions) forms the probe at the ionization plane, but the inelastically-scattered wave is then propagated to the exit by ordinary multislice per scan position – so the exit-leg cost still scales with the number of probe positions.

prism_transition_potential() is the proper dual-scattering-matrix algorithm (Brown & Ophus) and is the preferred entry point; this function is kept for the partitioned-PRISM path and as the equivalence oracle. The two return bit-for-bit-equivalent results (up to float rounding).

Parameters:

  • probe_q (Tensor) – Probe-forming aperture in reciprocal space (Ny, Nx) (complex).

  • transmissions (Tensor) – Real-space transmission functions (NZ, Ny, Nx).

  • transition_potentials (TransitionPotentials) – Transition potentials for the edge.

  • sites (ndarray) – Fractional (Nsite, 3) (y, x, z) coordinates of ionizable atoms.

  • scan_pixels (Tensor) – Scan positions (P, 2) in pixels.

  • wavelength – As in multislice_transition_potential().

  • gridsize – As in multislice_transition_potential().

  • slice_distance – As in multislice_transition_potential().

  • return_real_space (bool, optional) – If True, return the real-space exit-wave intensity instead of the diffraction-space intensity.

  • interpolation_factor (int or (int, int)) – PRISM interpolation factor f (or (fy, fx)); see ScatteringMatrix. 1 (default) is exact; f > 1 subsamples the beams to speed up the scattering matrix by f**2 and is accurate while the probe fits in the 1/f window.

  • partition (dict or None) – If given (e.g. {"n_radial": 4}), use a PartitionedScatteringMatrix (partitioned PRISM, Pelz 2021) instead; interpolation_factor is then ignored. None (default) uses the exact per-pixel scattering matrix.

Returns:

Intensity (P, Ny, Nx) summed over transitions and sites, per incident electron and per eV of energy loss: |fft2|^2 / (Ny Nx), or |psi|^2 with return_real_space.

Return type:

Tensor

scatterem.simulation.eels.prism_eels_image(probe_q: Tensor, transmissions: Tensor, transition_potentials: TransitionPotentials, sites: ndarray, scan_pixels: Tensor, *, wavelength: float, gridsize: Sequence[float], slice_distance: float, detector_mrad: float, interpolation_factor=1, inelastic_crop: int | None = None, prism_mask: bool = True, scan_shape: Sequence[int] | None = None, partition: dict | None = None, partition_s2: dict | None = None, qeels_axis: int | Literal['both'] | None = None, contract: Literal['auto', 'columns', 'probe'] = 'auto', mag_preserve: bool = True, focal_backprop: float | str | None = None, scan_chunk: int | None = 8192, reconstruction_workspace: int | None = None) → Tensor | tuple[Tensor, Tensor]#

Double-channeling PRISM STEM-EELS image I(x, y).

Parameters:

  • probe_q (Tensor (Ny, Nx)) – Probe-forming aperture in reciprocal space (complex).

  • transmissions (Tensor (NZ, Ny, Nx)) – Elastic transmission functions (|T| = 1; no absorption).

  • transition_potentials (TransitionPotentials) – Transition potentials (.array (n_trans, Ny, Nx), centred at origin).

  • sites (ndarray (Nsite, 3)) – Fractional (y, x, z) of the ionized atoms.

  • scan_pixels (Tensor (P, 2)) – Scan positions in pixels.

  • wavelength – As elsewhere.

  • gridsize – As elsewhere.

  • slice_distance – As elsewhere.

  • detector_mrad (float) – EELS detector collection semi-angle [mrad]; output beams within it.

  • interpolation_factor (int or (int, int)) – PRISM interpolation factor for S1 (and the scan crop region).

  • inelastic_crop (int, optional) – Crop the transition-potential / scattering-matrix window to (Ny, Nx) // inelastic_crop around each atom (the localized transition). None uses the full grid (exact; equals the detector-integrated 4D dual-S).

  • prism_mask (bool) – Restrict each atom’s contribution to scan positions within the PRISM 1/f crop region around it (matches the interpolation-factor periodicity).

  • scan_shape ((int, int), optional) – If given, the flat (P,) image is reshaped to scan_shape.

  • partition (dict, optional) – If given (e.g. {"n_radial": 4}), build S1 on Bp parent beams (PartitionedScatteringMatrix) and reconstruct the exact aperture columns on each atom’s crop window via natural-neighbor interpolation. This cheapens the S1 build/advance + memory (Bp parents) at the cost of the NNW reconstruction error. A "focal_backprop" key overrides the focal_backprop argument for S1. None uses the exact per-pixel S1. When one slice’s windows cover the grid, both partitioned legs reuse one full-grid reconstruction per slice, within the additional workspace that reconstruction_workspace sets; sparse windows and focal referencing stay windowed.

  • partition_s2 (dict, optional) – Same idea for S2 (the detector matrix): build the transpose multislice on Bp parent detector beams and NNW-reconstruct the detector columns on the crop window, shrinking the resident S2 from ndet to Bp columns at a second NNW error. "dechirp" (default True) removes and restores the scalar vacuum beam phase around the interpolation (see DetectorExitSMatrix); "focal_backprop" turns on the Fresnel referencing of S2 (off unless given here). None keeps the full per-beam S2.

  • qeels_axis ({0, 1, "both"}, optional) – Momentum-resolved (qEELS) output. None (default) returns the scalar elemental map. 0 or 1 resolves that detector-momentum axis and projects the perpendicular one away: each beam’s |amp_d|^2 is binned by its signed frequency along qeels_axis rather than summed over all d. "both" keeps every detector beam in its own bin (no projection). Summing the spectrum over its momentum axis returns the map to float64 round-off – the same additions, grouped differently, so the agreement is ~1 ULP (measured 2e-16 relative) rather than bitwise. Works with partition / partition_s2 (the binning is post-|amp|^2); for a faithful resolved axis use interpolation_factor == 1 along it.

  • contract ({"auto", "columns", "probe"}, default "auto") – How the per-atom contraction is associated (same result to rounding, different cost). "columns" forms the scan-independent (n_det, B) coupling S2c (H S1c) once per atom and applies the scan coefficients last; it is best when P is very large or the crop window is the full grid. "probe" synthesises the probe on the crop window first (probe = c S1c) and contracts it against the detector columns; it avoids the O(n_det B |window|) intermediate and is faster for small crop windows and modest P. "auto" picks the cheaper order per atom from the shapes (see _contract_orders).

  • mag_preserve (bool, default True) – Magnitude-preserving NNW reconstruction of the partitioned S1 and S2 columns: keep the complex sum’s phase but restore the interpolated magnitude. This counters the phase-decoherence amplitude loss of the plain complex average and converges to the exact result at full parents. False is the plain complex average. Ignored without partition / partition_s2.

  • focal_backprop (float, "centroid" or None, optional) – Fresnel referencing of the partitioned S1 parents: interpolate them at a plane back along the traversed depth, then propagate the reconstructed window forward again. "centroid" takes half the traversed depth and a number takes that fraction, rounded to whole slices. None (default) or 0 disables it. S2 uses referencing only when partition_s2 names it.

  • scan_chunk (int or None, default 8192) – Most scan positions one atom contracts at once. It bounds the scan-dependent intermediate memory, so the scan can be sampled arbitrarily finely. The result does not depend on the value (to rounding); None processes all positions of an atom in one block.

  • reconstruction_workspace (int or None, default None) – Additional device memory (bytes) that the partitioned legs may use to reuse one full-grid NNW reconstruction per slice. None uses the default of 2 GiB. 0 turns the reuse off: every atom reconstructs its own crop window, which is the behaviour of the BiP-PRISM paper and of v0.3, with the smallest peak memory. The result does not depend on the value (to rounding). Ignored without partition / partition_s2.

Returns:

With qeels_axis=None: the STEM-EELS image, (P,) or scan_shape, per incident electron and per eV (independent of the grid and of f). Otherwise (spectrum, q_pixels), where spectrum carries a trailing momentum axis ((P, n_q) or scan_shape + (n_q,)) and q_pixels is each bin’s sorted signed pixel frequency (physical q = q_pixels / gridsize[qeels_axis]). For "both", q_pixels is (n_q, 2) in (qy, qx) order, one signed pair per detector beam; divide each column by its grid size to get inverse Angstrom.

Return type:

Tensor or (Tensor, Tensor)

Raises:

ValueError – If contract or qeels_axis is not one of the listed values, or if reconstruction_workspace is negative.

class scatterem.simulation.eels.ScatteringMatrix(probe_q: Tensor, transmissions: Tensor, kernel: Tensor, interpolation_factor: Sequence[int] = (1, 1))#

Plane-wave scattering matrix \(\mathcal S\) advanced by multislice.

Each row is the multislice-propagated plane wave for one beam in the probe-forming aperture. Advancing the matrix to a given depth and forming a probe by linear combination reproduces the elastic wave at that depth for any scan position.

Parameters:

  • probe_q (Tensor) – Probe-forming aperture in reciprocal space (Ny, Nx) (complex; corner origin). Non-zero pixels define the beams.

  • transmissions (Tensor) – Real-space transmission functions (NZ, Ny, Nx).

  • kernel (Tensor) – Fresnel propagator (Ny, Nx) for one inter-slice distance.

  • interpolation_factor ((int, int), optional) – PRISM interpolation factors (fy, fx) (Ophus 2017); (1, 1) keeps every beam and is exact. See __init__() for the full anti-aliasing discussion.

class scatterem.simulation.eels.PartitionedScatteringMatrix(probe_q: Tensor, transmissions: Tensor, kernel: Tensor, n_radial: int = 4, n_angular: int = 6, interpolation_factor: Sequence[int] = (1, 1), focal_backprop: float | str | None = None, mag_preserve: bool = True, wavelength: float | None = None, slice_distance: float | None = None, gridsize: Sequence[float] | None = None)#

Partitioned-PRISM scattering matrix (Pelz 2021) for STEM-EELS.

Instead of one multislice-propagated plane wave per aperture pixel, the matrix is built on a small set of Bp parent beams (a hex-ring subsample of the aperture). The probe at a scan position is synthesised by natural- neighbor interpolation of the de-tilted parent columns:

psi(r, R) = sum_p S_dt[p](r) * basis_p(r - R), S_dt[p](r) = S[p](r) * exp(-2 pi i g_p . r / N), (de-tilted column) basis_p(rho) = sum_b coeffs[b] w[b,p] exp(2 pi i g_b . rho / N),

where w[b,p] are the natural-neighbor weights expressing aperture beam b in terms of the parents. In the full-parent limit (every beam its own parent, w the identity) this is algebraically the exact per-pixel probe, so ScatteringMatrix is the Bp -> B limit and serves as the oracle. Presents the advance_to / probe_at_current_plane interface of ScatteringMatrix plus coeffs_at() / reconstruct_columns(), so it can drive either the hybrid path or the dual-scattering-matrix exit (the reconstructed columns are scalar-combinable). Accepts interpolation_factor so PRISM beam subsampling composes with partitioning. Accuracy is regime-dependent (the natural-neighbor reconstruction error).

Parameters:

  • probe_q (Tensor) – Probe-forming aperture in reciprocal space (Ny, Nx) (complex; corner origin). Non-zero pixels define the beams.

  • transmissions (Tensor) – Real-space transmission functions (NZ, Ny, Nx).

  • kernel (Tensor) – Fresnel propagator (Ny, Nx) for one inter-slice distance.

  • n_radial (int, optional) – Number of concentric hex rings of parent beams sampled from the aperture (must be >= 2).

  • n_angular (int, optional) – Number of angular samples on the first hex ring (subsequent rings scale with ring index).

  • interpolation_factor ((int, int), optional) – PRISM interpolation factors (fy, fx) (Ophus 2017), applied to the aperture before partitioning; (1, 1) keeps every beam.

  • focal_backprop (float, str or None, optional) – Fresnel referencing of the parent columns before natural-neighbor fusion (Pelz 2021). A float back-propagates by that fraction of the traversed depth, rounded to whole slices; "centroid" selects half the traversed depth. The fused columns are then propagated forward to the current plane again. None (default) or 0 disables the referencing. It is skipped in the full-parent limit, where the columns are exact.

  • mag_preserve (bool, optional) – Restore each reconstructed column’s magnitude from the same NNW interpolation of |S|, keeping the complex sum’s phase. Applies to reconstruct_columns_window().

  • wavelength (float, optional) – Electron wavelength in Angstrom. With slice_distance and gridsize it sets the windowed Fresnel step that reconstruct_columns_window() needs when focal_backprop is on.

  • slice_distance (float, optional) – Slice distance in Angstrom (see wavelength).

  • gridsize ((float, float), optional) – Real-space grid extent (Ly, Lx) in Angstrom (see wavelength).

class scatterem.simulation.eels.DetectorExitSMatrix(det_idx: Tensor, transmissions: Tensor, kernel: Tensor, partition: dict | None = None, mag_preserve: bool = True, focal_backprop: float | str | None = None, wavelength: float | None = None, slice_distance: float | None = None, gridsize: Sequence[float] | None = None)#

S2: columns are detector-output beams back-propagated to the current slice.

S2_d(r) is the adjoint (transpose) multislice of the conjugate detector plane wave e_d* from the exit surface back to the current slice, so that for any wave w at that slice sum_r S2_d(r) w(r) == fft(forward_exit(w))[d] – the amplitude reaching detector beam d. Built once covering all slices (slice 0 -> exit) and peel_to() advances the start slice forward (removing front slices) so it is reused across every atom.

With partition the transpose multislice is built on only Bp parent detector beams (a hex-ring subsample); the full detector columns are NNW-reconstructed on a crop window via columns_window(). By reciprocity the de-tilted back-propagated columns are locally similar, so the same partitioned-PRISM interpolation applies – shrinking the resident S2 from ndet to Bp columns.

Parameters:

  • det_idx (Tensor) – Corner-origin pixel indices of the accepted detector beams, shape (ndet, 2), integer dtype.

  • transmissions (Tensor) – Per-slice transmission functions, shape (nz, ny, nx), complex dtype; determines the grid shape and the build device/dtype.

  • kernel (Tensor) – Fresnel propagator kernel for one slice step, shape (ny, nx), complex dtype.

  • partition (dict or None) – When given, enables partitioned (parent-beam) construction; recognized keys are "n_radial" and "n_angular", the hex-ring subsample resolution passed to the NNW weighting, and "dechirp" (default True), which removes each column’s accumulated vacuum propagator phase before the NNW combination and restores it per output beam afterwards. "dechirp": False is the ablation without it. None builds the full ndet columns directly.

  • mag_preserve (bool, default True) – Restore the magnitude of the partitioned reconstruction from the same NNW interpolation, keeping the complex sum’s phase. Ignored when partition is None (the columns are then exact).

  • focal_backprop (float, str or None, optional) – Fresnel referencing of the partitioned parents before interpolation: the parents are propagated toward the exit by that fraction of the remaining path nz - start ("centroid" is half of it, rounded to whole slices), combined on a padded window, and propagated back. None (default) or 0 disables it. It is skipped in the full-parent limit, where the columns are exact.

  • wavelength (float, optional) – Electron wavelength in Angstrom. With slice_distance and gridsize it sets the windowed Fresnel step that focal_backprop needs.

  • slice_distance (float, optional) – Slice distance in Angstrom (see wavelength).

  • gridsize ((float, float), optional) – Real-space grid extent (Ly, Lx) in Angstrom (see wavelength).

Elastic PRISM#

ScanExitWaveOperator

Map a transmission function, probe and scan positions to exit waves.

PrismScanOp

Scan-time exit-wave operator that projects a partitioned S-matrix.

MultisliceScanOp

Standard per-position multislice.

build_prism_smeta

Synthesize a pure- or partitioned-PRISM, f-lattice SMeta (Ophus 2017).

build_prism_smeta_for_probe

Power-based f-lattice-shell PRISM SMeta from the probe (faithful PRISM).
class scatterem.nn.scan_exit_wave.ScanExitWaveOperator(*args, **kwargs)#

Map a transmission function, probe and scan positions to exit waves.

Two flavours of T input, decided by wants_full_fov:

  • wants_full_fov = False – T is per-position patches of shape (NZ_bin, K, M1, M2); the operator runs an inner multislice-style loop over scan positions. This is the default multislice path.

  • wants_full_fov = True – T is the full-FOV transmission stack of shape (NZ_bin, NY, NX); the operator builds an S-matrix from it (via plane-wave multislice) and projects to scan positions cheaply. This is the PRISM / partitioned-PRISM path.

The probe is always given in real space (Nmodes, K, M1, M2); operators that need the Fourier-aperture form FFT internally.

exit_antialias_aperture (default None, and None on every reconstruction path) is the wave-side half of a band-limited forward that the Fresnel propagator cannot carry: the aperture applied once more after the last transmission, which the propagator only does BETWEEN slices. Each operator applies it through _bandlimit_exit() at its own exit point – the multislice loop on the exit wave, the PRISM family on the finished S-matrix columns – on the grid it hands the field back on.

Parameters:

  • *args (Any) – Forwarded to torch.nn.Module.__init__.

  • **kwargs (Any) – Forwarded to torch.nn.Module.__init__.

Variables:

exit_antialias_aperture (torch.Tensor or None) – Real (Ny, Nx) antialiasing aperture in FFT layout on the operator’s output grid, or None. A plain attribute, not a registered buffer, so it stays out of state_dict() and checkpoints written before it existed still load; being a plain attribute it is also NOT moved by .to(device) – _bandlimit_exit() moves it per call instead.

class scatterem.nn.scan_exit_wave.PrismScanOp(s_meta: SMeta, f: int | tuple = 1, freeze_s_matrix: bool = False, scan_chunk: int | None = None, periodic: bool = True, precision_config: dict | str | None = None, focal_backprop: float | str = 'centroid', use_warp: bool | None = None, build_cols: int | None = None)#

Scan-time exit-wave operator that projects a partitioned S-matrix.

Constructs an S-matrix on a set of parent beams (a subset of the aperture beams) and projects to each scan position via beamlet-weighted natural-neighbor sums.

Parameters:

  • s_meta (SMeta) – Beam/beamlet metadata (parent beams, weights, simulation grid).

  • f (int or tuple, optional) – Anisotropic interpolation factor (f_y, f_x); a scalar broadcasts to both axes.

  • freeze_s_matrix (bool, optional) – If True, detach the transmission before building the S-matrix.

  • scan_chunk (int or None, optional) – Chunk size for prism_project over scan positions.

  • periodic (bool, optional) – Whether prism_project treats the S-matrix as periodic.

  • precision_config (dict or str or None, optional) – Precision preset resolved by resolve_precision().

  • focal_backprop (float or str, optional) – Fraction of the thickness (0 = exit, 1 = entrance) to back-propagate parent columns to before NNW fusion, or "centroid" to auto-select the scattering centroid.

  • use_warp (bool or None, optional) – Whether to use the Warp kernel for scan synthesis; None follows the SCATTEREM_USE_WARP environment variable.

  • build_cols (int or None, optional) – Parent beams propagated at once in the S-matrix build (>= 1), capping its (cols, MY, MX) transients; None is one pass when the stack fits ~6e8 complex elements. SCATTEREM_PRISM_BUILD_COLS overrides.

class scatterem.nn.scan_exit_wave.MultisliceScanOp#

Standard per-position multislice.

Two transmission input flavours, selected by inverse_index:

  • inverse_index is None – T is already-gathered per-position patches of shape (NZ_bin, K, M1, M2); each slice is broadcast- multiplied into the waves.

  • inverse_index given – T is the ungathered per-unique-pixel (exponentiated) potential stack of shape (NZ_bin, U); the gather + complex multiply is fused per slice via the Warp fused_transmit kernel.

In both cases inter-slice Fresnel propagation is applied after every slice except the last (matching the model).

exit_antialias_aperture (inherited; default None, and None on every reconstruction path) optionally applies an antialiasing aperture once to the exit wave; see forward().

checkpoint_every (default 0, off) checkpoints the slice loop in segments of that many slices when a gradient is recorded (checkpointed_slice_loop in _slice_checkpoint): O(N_sl / s + s) activation memory for one extra forward, with the same output and gradients.

scatterem.nn.scan_exit_wave.build_prism_smeta(*, pixels: tuple[int, int], f: int | tuple[int, int], dx, wavelength: float, semiconvergence_angle: float, fov_shape: tuple[int, int] | None, device, n_radial: int | None = None, n_angular: int = 6, margin: float | None = None) → SMeta#

Synthesize a pure- or partitioned-PRISM, f-lattice SMeta (Ophus 2017).

Instance-free so the reconstruction path can reuse it for f>1 later (spec forward-compat): everything is taken from the explicit arguments, not from a simulator instance.

Parameters:

  • pixels ((int, int)) – Detector window (P_y, P_x). The simulation grid is N = f * pixels per axis; the detector is N / f = pixels (dk = f·Δq).

  • f (int) – PRISM interpolation factor (>= 1).

  • dx (array-like (2,)) – Real-space pitch Δp = unitcell / pixels per axis (Å). UNCHANGED by f – the N grid is the larger probe window at the same pitch.

  • wavelength (float) – Electron wavelength (Å).

  • semiconvergence_angle (float) – Probe semiconvergence angle (rad).

  • fov_shape ((int, int) or None) – Extent (NY_fov, NX_fov) of an object that has to FIT inside the simulation grid: a finite specimen, a reconstructed volume, or anything scanned with a non-periodic crop. Raises if f * pixels < FOV. None for a PERIODIC specimen under a periodic crop: the N grid is then the crystal itself and a window leaving it wraps onto the next cell, so there is nothing to fit – which is what lets PRISM at f = 1 scan at all.

  • device (torch.device or str) – Device the SMeta tensors are built on.

  • n_radial (int or None) – Partitioned-PRISM knob. None (the default) -> pure PRISM: every f-lattice beam is its own parent (the behavior below). When set, after the pure full-aperture SMeta is built it is replaced by SMeta.make_beamlet_meta(n_radial, n_angular), which selects Bp << B parent beams on n_radial (+ DC) hex rings and builds the Voronoi natural-neighbor weights (B, Bp) + beamlet basis (Bp, MY, MX).

  • n_angular (int) – Beamlet hex-ring angular sample count passed through to SMeta.make_beamlet_meta() (default 6). Ignored when n_radial is None.

  • margin (float or None) – None (the default): the beams are the support of the probe-forming aperture (_geometry.aperture_support), i.e. every Fourier coefficient the probe has. A number selects the legacy disk |k| <= margin * alpha / lambda instead, which truncates the aperture’s soft edge when the aperture is small in pixels (it was hard-coded at 1.05); kept for the reconstruction model’s prism_spec["aperture"] = "kmax_margin".

Returns:

When n_radial is None: a pure-PRISM SMeta on the N grid with an f-lattice BF-disk aperture, identity natural-neighbor weights and one-hot beamlets. When n_radial is set: the partitioned SMeta (parent-beam subset Bp << B, Voronoi NNW (B, Bp), beamlets (Bp, MY, MX)).

Return type:

SMeta

Raises:

ValueError – If f * pixels < FOV (object does not fit) – the message tells the caller to increase pixels so f * pixels >= scan_extent + detector.

scatterem.nn.scan_exit_wave.build_prism_smeta_for_probe(*, probe: Tensor, pixels: tuple[int, int], f: int, dx, wavelength: float, semiconvergence_angle: float, fov_shape: tuple[int, int], device, power_fraction: float = 0.9999, n_radial: int | None = None, n_angular: int = 6) → SMeta#

Power-based f-lattice-shell PRISM SMeta from the probe (faithful PRISM).

Sizes the BF-disk aperture from the incoherent multi-mode probe power spectrum instead of the fixed kmax*1.05 margin of build_prism_smeta(). The f-lattice only has beams at every f-th N-grid frequency pixel, so the candidate aperture radii are the f-lattice shells {0, f*dk, 2f*dk, ...} (dk = 1/(N*dx)). The chosen radius is the SMALLEST shell whose cumulative power reaches power_fraction of the total, floored at ``kmax*1.2`` so the aperture is never tighter than 1.2x the convergence angle. This captures the soft (tanh) probe-edge tail the fixed margin truncates – the too-tight-aperture footgun for f-lattice PRISM (Ophus 2017).

Self-contained and reusable by both the reconstruction and simulation paths (everything is taken from the explicit arguments, like build_prism_smeta()).

Parameters:

  • probe (Tensor) – Complex real-space probe of shape (Nmodes, MY, MX) on the N = f*pixels grid. The incoherent power spectrum P(k) = sum_m |FFT(probe[m])|^2 (sum over the mode axis) drives the aperture sizing. A single-mode (1, MY, MX) probe is fine.

  • pixels ((int, int)) – Detector window (P_y, P_x); the sim grid is N = f*pixels.

  • f (int) – PRISM interpolation factor (>= 1).

  • dx (array-like (2,)) – Real-space pitch Delta p per axis (Aa), UNCHANGED by f.

  • wavelength (float) – Electron wavelength (Aa).

  • semiconvergence_angle (float) – Probe semiconvergence angle (rad). kmax = semiconvergence_angle / wavelength sets the kmax*1.2 floor.

  • fov_shape ((int, int)) – Object FOV (NY_fov, NX_fov). Raises if f*pixels < FOV.

  • device (torch.device or str) – Device the SMeta tensors are built on.

  • power_fraction (float) – Target cumulative incoherent-power fraction the aperture must enclose (default 0.9999 – 99.99%).

  • n_radial (int or None) – Partitioned-PRISM knob, forwarded to SMeta.make_beamlet_meta (None -> pure PRISM).

  • n_angular (int) – Beamlet hex-ring angular sample count (default 6). Ignored when n_radial is None.

Returns:

The f-lattice BF-disk SMeta at the power-chosen radius (pure, or partitioned when n_radial is set), enclosing >= power_fraction of the incoherent probe power and never tighter than kmax*1.2.

Return type:

SMeta

Raises:

ValueError – If f*pixels < FOV (object does not fit), or the probe grid does not match N = f*pixels.

Propagation#

Propagator

Fresnel/angular-spectrum single-slice propagator for multislice simulation.

SubpixShift

Fourier-domain sub-pixel shift of a batch of probe wave fields.
class scatterem.nn.modules.Propagator(slice_thickness: float, wavelength: float, dx: float | Sequence[float] | ndarray, shape: tuple | Size | ndarray, device: str | device | None = 'cpu', method: str = 'angular_spectrum', tilt: Sequence[float] | None = None)#

Fresnel/angular-spectrum single-slice propagator for multislice simulation.

Precomputes a (MY, MX) transfer-function phase ramp for propagating a wave field by slice_thickness and applies it in forward() via an FFT round-trip. The ramp is built by propagator_kernel() (paraxial) or angular_spectrum_kernel() (exact).

Parameters:

  • slice_thickness (float) – Propagation distance per slice, in the same length units as dx.

  • wavelength (float) – Electron wavelength, in the same length units as dx.

  • dx (float or Sequence of float or numpy.ndarray) – Real-space pixel size, scalar or per-axis.

  • shape (tuple or torch.Size or numpy.ndarray) – Simulation grid shape (MY, MX).

  • device (str or torch.device or None, optional) – Device to build the phase ramp on.

  • method (str, optional) – "angular_spectrum"/"asm" (exact, default) or "fresnel"/"paraxial" (paraxial approximation).

  • tilt (Sequence of float or None, optional) – Global crystal tilt (theta_y, theta_x) in RADIANS (adaptive propagator ptychography, Sha et al. 2022). Multiplies prop by exp(+2*pi*i * dz * (qy*tan(theta_y) + qx*tan(theta_x))), PtyRAD’s kernel: the wave is translated by -dz*tan(theta) per slice, i.e. the object’s columns advance by +dz*tan(theta) per slice relative to the beam. Only the physical kernel prop carries it; the reference-plane fresnel_kernel()/fresnel_phase() stay untilted. None or all-zero leaves prop bit-identical.

class scatterem.nn.modules.SubpixShift(probe_shape: tuple | Size, device: str | device | None, subpix_shift: bool, rdtype: dtype = torch.float32)#

Fourier-domain sub-pixel shift of a batch of probe wave fields.

Shifts each wave by a per-position fractional offset dr via a linear phase ramp applied in the Fourier domain, so probe positions need not land on integer detector pixels.

Parameters:

  • probe_shape (tuple or torch.Size) – Probe tensor shape (a, b, MY, MX); only the detector-plane dimensions (MY, MX) are used to build the frequency ramps.

  • device (str or torch.device or None) – Device to build the frequency-ramp buffers on.

  • subpix_shift (bool) – Whether forward applies the sub-pixel shift; if False, forward only broadcasts waves to the batch of positions.

  • rdtype (torch.dtype, optional) – Real dtype of the stored frequency ramps. Default is torch.float32.

Slice transmission in ptychography#

multislice_transmit_slice

One multislice transmission + (optional) propagation step.
scatterem.nn.ptychography.multislice_transmit_slice(sample_patches: Tensor, waves: Tensor, propagator: Propagator | None, inverse_index: Tensor | None = None, gather_index: Tensor | None = None) → Tensor#

One multislice transmission + (optional) propagation step.

Module-level so every MultisliceScanOp route shares the EXACT same per-slice routine.

Parameters:

  • sample_patches (Tensor) – Per-slice transmission. When inverse_index is given this is the ungathered per-unique-pixel (exponentiated) potential [U] and the gather + complex multiply is fused in one Warp kernel; otherwise it is already gathered [K, ph, pw] and a plain broadcast multiply is used.

  • waves (Tensor) – Complex exit waves, shape Nmodes x K x M1 x M2.

  • propagator (Propagator or None) – Fresnel propagator, or None to skip inter-slice propagation (last slice in a stack / single-slice degenerate case).

  • inverse_index (Tensor, optional) – Per-pixel -> unique-pixel map, shape [K, ph, pw], for the fused Warp transmit path.

  • gather_index (Tensor, optional) – The same map for the torch route: sample_patches is then the ungathered [U] slice and is expanded HERE, one slice at a time, so no (NZ, K, ph, pw) copy of the transmission stack ever exists.

Returns:

Complex exit waves, shape Nmodes x K x M1 x M2.

Return type:

Tensor

scatterem.utils.stem.beamlet_samples(beam_mask: ArrayLike, radius: float, n_angular_samples: int = 6, n_radial_samples: int = 3) → ndarray#

Select PRISM beam coordinates closest to a polar sampling pattern.

Builds a set of target points on concentric rings (plus the origin) and, for each target, picks the nearest actual beam coordinate present in beam_mask.

Parameters:

  • beam_mask (array_like) – Boolean (or 0/1) FFT-shifted mask of shape (M, M) selecting which Fourier-space beams are available.

  • radius (float) – Outer radius, in pixel units, of the polar sampling pattern.

  • n_angular_samples (int, optional) – Number of angular samples on the innermost ring; later rings use a proportionally larger count. Default is 6.

  • n_radial_samples (int, optional) – Number of radial rings (including the origin). Default is 3.

Returns:

Integer (y, x) beam coordinates closest to each polar sample point, with shape (n_samples, 2).

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

scatterem.utils.stem.natural_neighbor_weights(known_points, interp_points, minimum_weight_cutoff=0.01, method='linear', device=None)#

Interpolation weights of interp_points on the sites known_points.

Every row is a partition of unity over the sites, exact at a site, and a point outside the sites’ convex hull takes weight 1 on its nearest site.

Parameters:

  • known_points ((B_S, 2) ndarray) – X, y-coordinates of observations.

  • interp_points ((B, 2) ndarray) – Coordinates of the grid points at which to calculate the interpolation.

  • minimum_weight_cutoff (float, optional) – Delete weights smaller than this cutoff. Default is 1e-2. Not applied by "sibson", which keeps every weight: dropping the small ones perturbs every other weight in the row and buys nothing.

  • method ({"linear", "sibson"}, optional) – "linear" (default) is the vectorised Delaunay-barycentric interpolation (_linear_barycentric_weights()): orders of magnitude faster than the Sibson loop, with the same partition-of-unity / exact-at-parents / nearest-fallback contract (piecewise-linear C0 rather than Sibson’s C1). "sibson" is natural-neighbour (area-stealing) interpolation, scatterem.utils.stem._sibson – smooth (C1), exact at the parents, and the scheme partitioned PRISM is named after.

  • device (str or torch.device, optional) – Only used by method="sibson": a CUDA device runs its Warp kernel there (2.5-4x faster, same weights to ~4e-15); None (default) or a CPU device runs NumPy. Pass it when the caller is already on the GPU.

Returns:

Weights for interpolating the grid locations from the B_S sampled points.

Return type:

(B, B_S) ndarray

scatterem.utils.stem.fftshift_checkerboard(ny: int, nx: int) → ndarray#

Build the +-1 checkerboard that is an fftshift in the conjugate domain.

Multiplying a field by -(-1) ** (i + j) shifts its transform by half the grid along both axes. That is a +-1 pattern only for EVEN sizes (an odd axis would need the complex ramp exp(-2 pi i k (n // 2) / n)), so odd sizes are refused here rather than answered with the wrong pattern.

Parameters:

  • ny (int) – Number of rows (must be even).

  • nx (int) – Number of columns (must be even).

Returns:

(ny, nx) array of alternating -1/+1 values, -1 at [0, 0].

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

Raises:

ValueError – If either size is odd.

Notes

Shapes are (ny, nx) here as everywhere else. Until 2026-09-18 the signature was (w, h) returning (h, w) while every caller passed (ny, nx), so a non-square probe grid raised a broadcast error.

Free-space propagation and probe shifts#

fourier_shift_stack

physics.fourier.fourier_shift for many shifts -> (P, *waves.shape).

propagate

One Fresnel propagation step (FFT · kernel · IFFT).

propagator_kernel

Fresnel free-space propagator exp(-i π λ Δz |q|²) (corner origin).

propagator_phase

Unwrapped free-space phase phi with kernel = exp(1j * phi).

angular_spectrum_kernel

Exact angular-spectrum free-space propagator exp(i dz (kz - k)).

transfer_phase

Free-space phase phi(|q|^2) of a propagation by dz.

tilt_phase

Per-slice phase 2*pi*dz*(qy*tan(theta_y) + qx*tan(theta_x)) [rad].
scatterem.physics.propagation.fourier_shift_stack(waves: Tensor, shifts: Tensor, phase_bytes: int = 134217728) → Tensor#

physics.fourier.fourier_shift for many shifts -> (P, *waves.shape).

Bitwise-identical to torch.stack([fourier_shift(waves, s) for s in shifts]) and much cheaper, for two reasons that have nothing to do with vectorised arithmetic:

  • fourier_shift reads each entry of a host shift with float(), so a loop over a scan on the GPU pays two device syncs per position – 2P pipeline stalls before any physics happens. Here the shifts stay on the device and there are none.

  • the loop recomputes fft2(waves) once per position; it is the same tensor every time, so it is hoisted.

Bitwise equality is why this is safe to drop in: the ramp is the same float64 elementwise arithmetic (a broadcast multiply against (P,1,1) shifts gives the same products as a scalar multiply per position), and cuFFT’s batched 2-D transform is bitwise independent per batch element – both verified over the scan geometries this path uses, not assumed.

The ramp is complex128 at (chunk, ny, nx), so it is chunked to phase_bytes rather than built for all P at once; the output is preallocated instead of torch.stack-ing a list, which halves the peak the loop form needed. The transform then writes into that preallocation via out=: assigning its result with out[a:b] = ifft2(...) allocates the whole chunk a second time and copies it, which is 6.9 % of this call at the shapes a scan uses.

fftfreq comes from _fftfreq_f64’s memo because it is a constant of the shape and this function is called once per scan batch (32 times per image on the benchmark), another 1.9 %. wq = fft2(waves) is constant per probe across those same calls, but hoisting it needs a cache keyed on tensor identity and lifetime, and it is measured at only 1.2 % – left alone deliberately.

It is written as polar(1, u) rather than exp(-2j*pi*t) because the two are the same bits and the second is strictly more work: the exponent’s real part is -0.0 for every element, so a complex exp spends one of its three float64 transcendentals computing exp(-0.0) == 1.0 and then multiplying by it, and the -2j*pi*t operand has to be materialised as a complex128 plane (32 B/element) to say so. polar takes the float64 angle directly and calls only cos/sin – which is what exp reduces to here – so the identity is exact, not approximate: verified torch.equal over the real scan, integer +-300 px, random fractional, zero and 1e-9 shifts, into complex64 and complex128 (0 differing float32 words of 4.2 M each). Do NOT go further and factor the ramp as exp(-2j*pi*ky*sy) * exp(-2j*pi*kx*sx): separability is nearly exact and moves 1.3e5 float32 words on this scan, which breaks the sha256 contracts the r7_eels target is gated on.

On CUDA at complex64 the whole ramp is one Warp kernel instead (_ramp_fused.ramp_phase_fused), which is bit-exact and 1.47x on a probe-build benchmark. The four eager passes above write 72 bytes per element to produce 8, but that traffic is NOT what the kernel is buying: polar is bound by double-precision sin/cos, not by memory (measured, cos(u) alone 0.1556 ms + sin(u) alone 0.1546 == polar’s 0.300), and a fused kernel that merely deletes the other three passes is worth only 1.029x. What pays is that sincos() performs ONE Payne-Hanek argument reduction for the pair where two separate calls perform two – and at the angles a scan uses (|u| up to 804, the shifts being hundreds of pixels) that reduction is the expensive half. See _ramp_fused.py, whose docstring names the three spellings that keep it bit-exact and the reason the launch needs an explicit stream=. The kernel that runs is the certified float-float one in _ramp_df.py, with the same bits. On the single-chunk power-of-two route with 2-D waves, that kernel also applies wq * before its store, again with the same bits.

ifft2’s own 1/N normalisation is torch’s, not cuFFT’s – the C2C plan is unnormalised, so norm="backward" (the default) is paid as a separate full-size pass over the (chunk, ny, nx) output. On this row that pass is 1.63 ms = 11.8 % of the whole device time and it exists only to multiply by a constant. When ny*nx is an exact power of two, 1/N is an exponent decrement, so it commutes bit-for-bit with every multiply and add in the transform and can ride on wq – ONE small (ny, nx) plane per call – leaving the inverse unnormalised. Two things are load-bearing and neither works alone (both measured; 0.995x and 1.001x respectively):

  • the fold needs the out= to go, because torch fuses the normalisation into the out-variant’s copy, so norm="forward" on its own merely turns a fused scalar-multiply into a plain copy_ of the same 2 x 16 MiB;

  • dropping out= needs the fold, because without it the normalisation pass is still there, just writing into a fresh allocation instead of a slice.

Together they are 1.124x on this row (and drop its peak 561 -> 545 MiB, the preallocation no longer existing), re-measured over six alternating separately-launched arms; the small and fine rows are a sub-bar 1.7 % and 3.8 %, same sign, and carry no claim. Only the single-chunk case takes it – which is every caller in this package at every registered size, chunk being 128 against a scan batch of 32 – because a multi-chunk call still needs the preallocation and the fold buys nothing there. The power-of-two test is an exactness condition, not a tuned one: at a non-power-of-two N the pre-scaling rounds where the post-scaling did not, which would move the sha256 contracts r7_eels is gated on. Verified as bytes over the real scan: 0 of 134 217 728 int32 words differ. (The one regime it would not be exact in is |fft2(waves)| < 2^-126 * N ~ 8e-34, where the scaled plane goes subnormal; a normalised wave function is 24 orders of magnitude clear of that – min|wq| is 6.3e-10 on this row – and testing for it would cost a device sync per call, i.e. more than the pass being removed.)

Parameters:

  • waves (Tensor) – Complex real-space waves (..., ny, nx).

  • shifts (Tensor) – (P, 2) shifts (sy, sx) in pixels, on any device.

  • phase_bytes (int, optional) – Byte budget of one complex128 ramp chunk (default 1 << 27).

Returns:

(P, *waves.shape): waves shifted by each row of shifts.

Return type:

Tensor

scatterem.physics.propagation.propagate(waves: Tensor, kernel: Tensor) → Tensor#

One Fresnel propagation step (FFT · kernel · IFFT).

For a large beam stack (the un-tiled 20 nm S-walk: (Bp, MY, MX) ~27 GB) the naive round-trip holds waves + the FFT result + the IFFT result (~3x27 GB) -> OOM on 80 GB. Beam-chunk the round-trip IN PLACE so only one chunk’s FFT transient is live. The 2-D FFT is independent per beam (fft2(waves)[b] == fft2(waves[b])), so the chunked in-place result is byte-identical to the single call. In-place is gated to the no-grad (forward-sim) path; recon keeps the out-of-place round-trip.

The inverse transform runs UNNORMALISED (norm="forward") with the 1/(MY*MX) folded into the propagator instead: torch applies the default norm="backward" as a separate full-tensor rescale of the (B, MY, MX) result, whereas riding on the kernel costs one pass over a single (MY, MX) plane – and, via _scaled_propagator()’s memo, only on the first call for a given propagator rather than on every slice. This step is memory-bandwidth-bound (the broadcast multiply alone runs at 87.6 % of this card’s peak), so that removed pass is ~16 % of it. Deliberately NOT folded into propagator_kernel: that is public API, and _detector_exit._conj_propagate normalises its own inverse transform with the same kernel.

Do NOT try to fold this round trip onto waves with out=. Both torch.fft.fft2(w, out=w) and out= into a distinct buffer are bit-exact, but torch’s CUDA out-variant transforms into a fresh allocation and copies into out, so each one costs a full extra read+write of the stack: at the r7_eels/wide/conventional shape (2048 x 192 x 192 complex128, 1152 MiB) the round trip goes 37.5 -> 41.3 ms for one out= and 44.9 for two, and the row goes 710.6 -> 914.5 ms.

Parameters:

  • waves (Tensor) – Complex real-space waves (..., MY, MX). A 3-D stack outside autograd is transformed IN PLACE and returned; otherwise a new tensor is.

  • kernel (Tensor) – Fresnel propagator (MY, MX) for one step (see propagator_kernel()), corner origin.

Returns:

The propagated waves, same shape and dtype as waves.

Return type:

Tensor

scatterem.physics.propagation.angular_spectrum_kernel(gpts: Sequence[int], gridsize: Sequence[float], wavelength: float, dz: float, device=None, dtype: dtype = torch.complex64) → Tensor#

Exact angular-spectrum free-space propagator exp(i dz (kz - k)).
